B14C001.summary: After the great war, Yudhishthira collapses in grief on the bank of the Ganga, and his brothers gather around him. Dhritarashtra tries to comfort him, admitting that he and Gandhari have the greater cause to mourn because he ignored Vidura's warnings about Duryodhana. The chapter opens the Aswamedhika Parva by setting Yudhishthira's despair at the centre of the story.

scenes.B14C001S01: Yudhishthira collapses by the Ganga, the Pandavas gather around him, and Dhritarashtra consoles him while confessing his own failure to heed Vidura.

shots.B14C001S01H02: Invocation to Narayana, Nara and Saraswati, with the word Jaya to be spoken.
shots.B14C001S01H03: Yudhishthira, overcome, falls by the Ganga; Krishna and Bhima lift him, and the brothers sit around him. Dhritarashtra urges him to rise and rule, and recalls Vidura's advice he rejected, ending with his own regret.

B14C002.summary: Krishna urges Yudhishthira to put aside grief, honour the dead with sacrifices and gifts, and carry out his duties as a king. Yudhishthira answers that he wants to leave for the forest because he feels guilty for killing Bhishma and Karna. Vyasa rebukes him for clinging to confused sorrow and reminds him of the teachings he has already received.

scenes.B14C002S01: Krishna advises Yudhishthira to act as a king and perform rites; Yudhishthira asks to retire to the forest; Vyasa rebukes him.

shots.B14C002S01H01: Vaisampayana reports that Dhritarashtra's words have calmed Yudhishthira, and that Krishna then advises him: excessive grief harms the dead, so he should perform sacrifices, feed the gods, the ancestors and guests, and give to the needy, since his duty is done.

B14C003.summary: Vyasa tells Yudhishthira that no one acts by his own power and that sins can be cleansed through sacrifice, penance and gifts. He urges him to prepare the Rajasuya and the horse sacrifice. Yudhishthira objects that the war has left him with no wealth for gifts, and that Duryodhana emptied the treasury, so Vyasa points to a hidden store of gold left by Brahmanas at Marutta's sacrifice.

scenes.B14C003S01: Vyasa argues for sacrifice as a cure for sin; Yudhishthira says he cannot pay for it; Vyasa names Marutta's buried gold as the remedy and Yudhishthira asks for its history.

shots.B14C003S01H01: Vyasa tells Yudhishthira that sins are removed by penance, sacrifice and gifts, and urges him to hold the Rajasuya and the horse sacrifice as earlier kings did.

B14C004.summary: Yudhishthira asks Vyasa to tell him about the royal sage Marutta. Vyasa traces the royal line from Manu through Ikshvaku, Vinsa and Vivinsa to Karandhama, Avikshit and finally Marutta, who held a great sacrifice on Mount Meru. The chapter gives the family background needed to explain where Marutta's gold came from.

scenes.B14C004S01: Yudhishthira requests the story of Marutta, and Vyasa begins a genealogy of the royal line, ending with Marutta's golden sacrifice on Mount Meru.

shots.B14C004S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Vyasa to recount the history of the royal sage Marutta.
shots.B14C004S01H02: Vyasa lists the ancestors from Manu down to Marutta, including the sons of Vinsa and Karandhama, and describes Marutta's sacrifice on Mount Meru with golden vessels.

B14C005.summary: Yudhishthira asks how Marutta grew so powerful and so rich. Vyasa describes the rivalry between Vrihaspati, Indra's priest, and his brother Samvarta, and how Marutta's growing power angered Indra. Indra asks Vrihaspati to stop serving Marutta, but Vrihaspati refuses to serve a mortal king, and Indra's envy is set aside.

scenes.B14C005S01: Yudhishthira asks about Marutta's wealth; Vyasa describes Indra's jealousy and Vrihaspati's refusal to abandon Indra's side for Marutta; Indra is calmed and goes home.

shots.B14C005S01H01: Yudhishthira asks how Marutta gained his power and gold, where that wealth is now, and how it could be recovered.
shots.B14C005S01H02: Vyasa tells of the quarrel between Vrihaspati and his brother Samvarta, Vrihaspati's rise as Indra's priest, Marutta's power, Indra's demand that Vrihaspati abandon Marutta, and Vrihaspati's refusal.
shots.B14C005S01H03: Vaisampayana reports that Indra's envy ends after Vrihaspati's reply, and that Indra praises him and returns home.

B14C006.summary: Marutta asks Vrihaspati to serve as his priest, but Vrihaspati refuses because he serves only the gods. Marutta despairs until Narada tells him to find Samvarta, who wanders near Varanasi in the guise of a madman. Following Narada's instructions, Marutta sets a corpse at the city gate, pursues Samvarta, endures his abuse and at last wins his attention under a fig tree, which sets up Samvarta's acceptance of the sacrifice.

scenes.B14C006S01: Vyasa introduces the legend; Marutta asks Vrihaspati to be his priest, and Vrihaspati refuses on the grounds that he serves only the Immortals; Narada then finds the troubled king.
scenes.B14C006S02: Marutta tells Narada of his rebuff and despair; Narada points him to Samvarta, who would perform the sacrifice if pleased.
scenes.B14C006S03: Narada gives Marutta the method for finding Samvarta; Marutta leaves a corpse at the gate, follows the sage, is smeared with filth, persists, and Samvarta finally rests under a fig tree.

shots.B14C006S01H01: Vyasa introduces the old legend of Vrihaspati and Marutta, and says Marutta prepared a sacrifice after Vrihaspati's earlier agreement with Indra and asks him to officiate.
shots.B14C006S01H02: Vrihaspati says he cannot serve Marutta because he has promised Indra to serve him.
shots.B14C006S01H03: Marutta reminds Vrihaspati that he is the family priest and should officiate at his sacrifice.
shots.B14C006S01H04: Vrihaspati replies that he has served only the Immortals and will not serve mortal men, so Marutta must find another priest.
shots.B14C006S01H05: Vyasa describes Marutta returning home in despair, meeting Narada, who greets him and asks what troubles him.
shots.B14C006S02H01: Vaisampayana says Marutta told Narada about the rebuff from Vrihaspati.
shots.B14C006S02H02: Marutta says he no longer wishes to live, since Vrihaspati's refusal has left him stained with sin.
shots.B14C006S02H03: Vyasa says Narada's reply revives Marutta.
shots.B14C006S02H04: Narada tells Marutta that Samvarta, Angira's son, wanders the earth naked, and that Samvarta could perform the sacrifice if he is pleased with him.
shots.B14C006S02H05: Marutta feels restored and asks where Samvarta can be found and how he can win his protection.
shots.B14C006S03H01: Narada explains that Samvarta wanders near Varanasi as a madman, and tells Marutta to place a corpse at the city gate, follow the man who turns away, and seek his protection; if Samvarta asks who sent him, he should name Narada, and if asked to follow Narada, say Narada has entered the fire.
shots.B14C006S03H02: Marutta follows Narada's instructions, leaves a corpse at the gate, and follows Samvarta, who covers him with filth and spittle. Marutta persists until Samvarta, tired, sits to rest under a fig tree.

B14C007.summary: Marutta finds Samvarta, who questions him and then, raving like a madman, refuses to perform the sacrifice until Marutta first asks Vrihaspati's permission. Marutta explains that Vrihaspati turned him away because Indra forbade it, and that he now wants Samvarta's help even at great cost. Samvarta agrees on condition that Marutta stays steadfast, so the sacrifice goes ahead with a new priest.

scenes.B14C007S01: Samvarta asks how Marutta found him and whether Narada sent him; Samvarta, pretending to be mad, refuses and says Marutta must go back to Vrihaspati first.
scenes.B14C007S02: Marutta explains Vrihaspati's refusal and swears loyalty; Samvarta demands his steadfastness and agrees to officiate.

shots.B14C007S01H01: Samvarta asks how Marutta came to know him and warns that a lie will split his head.
shots.B14C007S01H02: Marutta says Narada told him that Samvarta is the son of their family priest.
shots.B14C007S01H03: Samvarta confirms the message and asks where Narada is now.
shots.B14C007S01H04: Marutta says Narada has entered the fire after commending him to Samvarta.
shots.B14C007S01H05: Vyasa describes Samvarta pleased but raving, claiming his brother has gone over to Indra and taken his goods, and telling Marutta to seek Vrihaspati's permission first.
shots.B14C007S02H01: Marutta explains that Vrihaspati refused because Indra forbade him to serve Marutta, and that he now wants Samvarta's help and will spend his wealth on it.
shots.B14C007S02H02: Samvarta agrees on condition that Marutta stays steadfast, fearing the anger of Vrihaspati and Indra.
shots.B14C007S02H03: Marutta swears that he will never abandon Samvarta.
shots.B14C007S02H04: Samvarta accepts, promising to make the sacrifice's rewards lasting and to raise Marutta nearly to Indra's level.

B14C008.summary: Samvarta sends Marutta to Mount Munjaban in the Himalayas, where Shiva dwells with Uma and his followers, and where gold mines are guarded by Kubera's attendants. Marutta is told to propitiate Shiva by his many names to obtain the gold. Marutta follows this advice and prepares a lavish sacrifice, but Vrihaspati grows sick with envy as he hears of it and Indra goes to comfort him.

scenes.B14C008S01: Samvarta describes Shiva's mountain and tells Marutta to worship Shiva for the gold; Marutta prepares the sacrifice, and Vrihaspati falls ill with envy.

shots.B14C008S01H01: Samvarta describes Munjaban, Shiva's mountain with its gold mines and guardians, and tells Marutta to worship Shiva by his many names to obtain the gold; Marutta does so and prepares the sacrifice, and Vrihaspati, distressed by the rival's prosperity, grows pale and sick, and Indra comes to him.

B14C009.summary: Indra finds Vrihaspati pale and distressed, and Vrihaspati blames Marutta's sacrifice, with Samvarta as its priest, and asks Indra to stop it. Indra sends Agni to present Vrihaspati to Marutta, but Marutta insists on Samvarta, and Samvarta threatens to burn Agni with his eyes if he comes again. Indra orders Agni back with a threat of his thunderbolt, but Agni refuses and recalls how Chyavana once overpowered Indra, so the conflict escalates.

scenes.B14C009S01: Indra asks Vrihaspati why he is in pain; Vrihaspati says his rival's sacrifice and Samvarta's role trouble him, and Indra dismisses the worry.
scenes.B14C009S02: Vrihaspati asks Indra to restrain his rival; Indra sends Agni, who sets out and reaches Marutta, who greets him as the fire-god.
scenes.B14C009S03: Agni delivers Indra's offer to present Vrihaspati; Marutta asks about the gods and refuses, insisting that Samvarta be his priest.
scenes.B14C009S04: Samvarta threatens to burn Agni with his evil eyes if he returns; Agni reports the failure to Indra, who orders him back with a threat.
scenes.B14C009S05: Agni refuses to go again, and Indra boasts of his power; Agni recalls how the sage Chyavana overcame Indra and the demon Mada, and says he will not oppose Samvarta.

shots.B14C009S01H01: Indra asks Vrihaspati whether he sleeps well, whether his servants are pleasing, and whether the gods protect him.
shots.B14C009S01H02: Vrihaspati says all is well in his own household and that the gods care for him.
shots.B14C009S01H03: Indra asks why Vrihaspati looks pale and in pain, and offers to kill whoever is harming him.
shots.B14C009S01H04: Vrihaspati says Marutta's great sacrifice, with Samvarta as priest, is what troubles him, and asks that Samvarta not officiate.
shots.B14C009S01H05: Indra says Vrihaspati already has all he could want as the gods' priest and asks what Samvarta could do to him now.
shots.B14C009S02H01: Vrihaspati says a rival's prosperity pains him, and asks Indra to restrain Samvarta and Marutta.
shots.B14C009S02H02: Indra tells Agni to take Vrihaspati to Marutta and promise that Vrihaspati will officiate and make him immortal.
shots.B14C009S02H03: Agni agrees to act as the messenger and sets out.
shots.B14C009S02H04: Vyasa describes Agni racing through the forests like a strong wind.
shots.B14C009S02H05: Marutta sees Agni arrive and asks the sage to offer him a seat, water and a cow.
shots.B14C009S03H01: Agni accepts the hospitality and identifies himself as Indra's messenger.
shots.B14C009S03H02: Marutta asks whether Indra is happy, pleased with him, and whether the other gods remain loyal.
shots.B14C009S03H03: Agni says Indra is content and wants to free Marutta from old age, then delivers the offer that Vrihaspati will serve as priest and grant immortality.
shots.B14C009S03H04: Marutta refuses, saying Samvarta will be his priest, since Vrihaspati has served Indra and should not serve mortals.
shots.B14C009S03H05: Agni promises that with Vrihaspati as priest Marutta would win the highest heavens and every realm.
shots.B14C009S04H01: Samvarta tells Agni never to bring Vrihaspati again, threatening to burn him with his fierce eyes.
shots.B14C009S04H02: Vyasa says Agni, trembling, returns to the gods, where Indra sees him with Vrihaspati and asks what happened.
shots.B14C009S04H03: Indra asks Agni whether Marutta accepted the message.
shots.B14C009S04H04: Agni reports that Marutta refused, clung to Vrihaspati, and insisted on Samvarta as priest.
shots.B14C009S04H05: Indra tells Agni to go back and threaten Marutta with a thunderbolt if he still refuses.
shots.B14C009S05H01: Agni refuses to go and suggests that Indra send a Gandharva, recalling Samvarta's furious threat.
shots.B14C009S05H02: Indra says no one can match Agni's power and that his words carry no weight.
shots.B14C009S05H03: Agni says that Indra, for all his power, could not prevent Vritra from taking his sovereignty.
shots.B14C009S05H04: Indra boasts of defeating his foes and says no one can live in peace after provoking him.
shots.B14C009S05H05: Agni recalls how the sage Chyavana, at the sacrifice of Saryati, fought Indra, and how Indra had to seek the sage's protection; Agni concludes that Brahmanas are stronger and he will not oppose Samvarta.

B14C010.summary: Indra threatens Marutta with his thunderbolt unless he accepts Vrihaspati as priest, and sends the Gandharva Dhritarashtra to carry the message. Marutta refuses, saying it would be a sin to break faith with Samvarta and that Vrihaspati should serve Indra instead. Samvarta calms the storm with incantations and summons Indra, who arrives, drinks the Soma, and is reconciled. Marutta gives away the gold, and Vyasa tells Yudhishthira that he should gather the same kind of gold for his own sacrifice.

scenes.B14C010S01: Indra sends Dhritarashtra, a Gandharva, with a threat; Marutta refuses and the Gandharva warns him that the thunderbolt is coming.
scenes.B14C010S02: Marutta asks Samvarta for protection; Samvarta promises to calm the storm and offers Marutta a boon.
scenes.B14C010S03: Marutta asks that Indra come to the sacrifice in person; Samvarta summons him by incantation, and Indra arrives and drinks the Soma.
scenes.B14C010S04: Indra praises Samvarta and orders the sacrifice's preparations; Marutta distributes gold to the Brahmanas, and Vyasa tells Yudhishthira to gather the same gold and sacrifice; Yudhishthira consults his ministers.

shots.B14C010S01H01: Indra tells Dhritarashtra to deliver to Marutta the demand that he accept Vrihaspati, or be struck with the thunderbolt.
shots.B14C010S01H02: Vyasa says Dhritarashtra goes to Marutta's court and delivers Indra's message.
shots.B14C010S01H03: Dhritarashtra, a Gandharva, introduces himself and repeats Indra's threat to strike Marutta with the thunderbolt unless he takes Vrihaspati as priest.
shots.B14C010S01H04: Marutta refuses, saying that breaking faith with a friend is as grave as killing a Brahmana, and that Vrihaspati should serve Indra while Samvarta serves him.
shots.B14C010S01H05: The Gandharva warns that Indra's war cry can be heard in the sky and that Indra will strike openly, so Marutta should think of his safety.
shots.B14C010S02H01: Vyasa says that after hearing the threat, Marutta tells Samvarta about it.
shots.B14C010S02H02: Marutta says that the thunder clouds mean Indra is near, asks Samvarta to protect him, and says his assistants are frightened.
shots.B14C010S02H03: Samvarta promises to calm the danger with his incantations and says Agni will protect Marutta.
shots.B14C010S02H04: Marutta says the crashing thunder and winds terrify him and have disturbed his peace of mind.
shots.B14C010S02H05: Samvarta promises to still the thunder with the winds and offers Marutta any boon he desires.
shots.B14C010S03H01: Marutta asks that Indra come to the sacrifice in person and accept his offerings, along with the other gods.
shots.B14C010S03H02: Samvarta says that, by his incantations, he has drawn Indra to the sacrifice, and the gods are hastening there.
shots.B14C010S03H03: Indra arrives in his chariot, drinks the Soma offered by Marutta, and is welcomed with honour.
shots.B14C010S03H04: Samvarta welcomes Indra, says the sacrifice has been made grand, and asks him to drink the Soma again.
shots.B14C010S03H05: Marutta thanks Indra for coming and says that Samvarta, Vrihaspati's younger brother, performs his sacrifice.
shots.B14C010S04H01: Indra says he knows Samvarta, whom he invited, and that his resentment against Marutta is gone.
shots.B14C010S04H02: Samvarta asks Indra to give the directions for the sacrifice and assign the shares of the gods, so the world knows it was done by Indra.
shots.B14C010S04H03: Vyasa says Indra orders the gods to build the hall and the rooms, and to prepare the sacrifice; the gods carry out the work, and Samvarta offers the oblations, after which the gods drink Soma and return home. Marutta gives gold to the Brahmanas and fills his treasury, and Vyasa tells Yudhishthira to gather the same gold and perform the sacrifice.
shots.B14C010S04H04: Vaisampayana says that Yudhishthira is delighted by Vyasa's words and begins to consult his ministers about his sacrifice.

B14C011.summary: Vasudeva (Krishna) sees Yudhishthira crushed by grief and tells him an old story. Vritra seized the earth's smell, the waters' liquid, light's colour, air's touch and ether's sound, and finally entered Indra's own body, leaving him confused until Vasishtha comforted him and Indra slew Vritra from within. Krishna presents the tale as a warning that the real enemies lie within, which prepares the ground for his teaching on the inner struggle.

scenes.B14C011S01: Krishna, seeing Yudhishthira grieving, begins a speech and recounts Indra's war with Vritra as a lesson about hidden enemies.

shots.B14C011S01H01: Vaisampayana says that after Vyasa's speech, Krishna sees the grieving Yudhishthira and addresses him.
shots.B14C011S01H02: Krishna tells the story of Indra's war with Vritra, in which Vritra drains one quality after another from the elements and finally from Indra, until Indra is saved and kills Vritra with an unseen thunderbolt.

B14C012.summary: Vasudeva (Krishna) explains that bodily and mental ailments both arise from the interplay of body and mind, and that the three qualities of the mind must stay in balance for health. He reminds Yudhishthira of past hardships, including the insult to Draupadi, the exile, and the fights with Drona and Bhishma, and says that Yudhishthira must now fight a battle alone against his own mind. The chapter moves from medicine to a call to self-discipline and to ruling well.

scenes.B14C012S01: Krishna explains the causes of illness, lists the troubles Yudhishthira has faced, and tells him to face his own mind and then rule the kingdom.

shots.B14C012S01H01: Krishna explains physical and mental ailments and the balance of humours and qualities, reminds Yudhishthira of his past sufferings, and says he must now overcome his own mind alone before governing his kingdom.

B14C013.summary: Vasudeva (Krishna) teaches that salvation comes from giving up attachment to the body's pleasures, not from merely renouncing external possessions. He sets death against the eternal Brahman and describes desire as the root of worldly attachment. He then recites the Kamagita, in which Desire itself explains that it cannot be destroyed by prayer, sacrifice, learning, truth or asceticism, since it takes many disguises. Krishna concludes that Yudhishthira should turn his desires toward virtue, perform the horse sacrifice, and stop grieving for the dead.

scenes.B14C013S01: Krishna teaches that death and eternal Brahman are the two forces within every creature; he recites the Kamagita, in which Desire boasts of its disguises, and then urges Yudhishthira to turn his desires to virtue and sacrifice.

shots.B14C013S01H01: Krishna teaches that salvation depends on giving up attachment to bodily pleasures, explains death and the eternal spirit, recites the Kamagita with Desire's boast of its disguises, and urges Yudhishthira to offer the horse sacrifice and stop grieving.

B14C014.summary: Yudhishthira is consoled by the sages, including Vyasa and Narada, and by his brothers, Draupadi and Arjuna, and his grief lifts. He performs funeral rites for Bhishma, Karna and the other fallen Kauravas, gives gifts to the Brahmanas, and asks the sages to guide him to the Himalayas for the sacrifice. The sages vanish, and Yudhishthira returns to Hastinapura with Dhritarashtra and continues to rule with his brothers.

scenes.B14C014S01: The sages comfort Yudhishthira; he performs funeral rites, gives gifts, returns to Hastinapura with Dhritarashtra, and goes on ruling with his brothers.

shots.B14C014S01H01: Vaisampayana reports that Yudhishthira is consoled by the sages and his family, performs the funeral rites and gifts, asks for guidance to the Himalayas for the sacrifice, and returns to Hastinapura with Dhritarashtra to rule with his brothers.

B14C015.summary: Janamejaya asks what Vasudeva and Arjuna did after the Pandavas regained their kingdom. Vaisampayana says the two travel happily and talk in the assembly hall at Indraprastha, and that Krishna comforts the grieving Arjuna. Krishna then says his work is done and asks Arjuna to tell Yudhishthira that he must return to Dwaravati, and Arjuna sorrowfully agrees, which marks the close of their time together.

scenes.B14C015S01: Janamejaya asks what Krishna and Arjuna did; Vaisampayana describes their travels and Krishna's consolation of Arjuna; Krishna asks Arjuna to tell Yudhishthira he will leave for Dwaravati, and Arjuna agrees.

shots.B14C015S01H01: Janamejaya asks Vaisampayana what Vasudeva and Dhananjaya did once the Pandavas had regained and pacified their kingdom.
shots.B14C015S01H02: Vaisampayana describes the two travelling in pleasure, recalling the war at Indraprastha, and Krishna comforting Arjuna, who finds relief.
shots.B14C015S01H03: Krishna says the kingdom is now secure under Yudhishthira and asks Arjuna to tell the king he is leaving for Dwaravati; Arjuna sorrowfully agrees.

B14C016.summary: Janamejaya asks what Krishna and Arjuna discussed after the victory, and Arjuna admits he has forgotten much of Krishna's earlier teaching from the battlefield and asks to hear it again. Krishna says the teaching cannot be repeated in full and instead tells an older tale of a sage named Kasyapa, who visited an emancipated Brahmana and served him. That Brahmana recounts his many lives of sorrow and how he took refuge in the Formless, which set up the Anugita's account of liberation.

scenes.B14C016S01: Janamejaya asks about Krishna and Arjuna's talk; Arjuna says he forgot Krishna's teaching and asks for it again, and Krishna offers to tell an older story instead.
scenes.B14C016S02: Kasyapa serves an emancipated Brahmana, who tells him of the many sorrows he endured across lives and of how he gave up the world for the Formless.

shots.B14C016S01H02: Janamejaya asks what Krishna and Arjuna talked about once they returned to the assembly rooms after their victory.
shots.B14C016S01H03: Vaisampayana describes Arjuna enjoying his recovered kingdom with Krishna in a palace, and Arjuna saying he has forgotten Krishna's teaching from the battle and asks to hear it again.
shots.B14C016S01H04: Vaisampayana says Krishna embraces Arjuna and prepares to reply.
shots.B14C016S01H05: Krishna says that he cannot fully repeat the earlier teaching, and offers instead an old story of a Brahmana visitor from the heavenly regions to set out the same truths.
shots.B14C016S02H01: The Brahmana introduces the story: the sage Kasyapa, seeking merit, comes to an accomplished Brahmana who has mastered the mysteries of religion and serves him as a disciple.
shots.B14C016S02H02: The accomplished Brahmana says that worldly rewards are temporary, describes his own many births and sorrows, and tells how he took refuge in the Formless and found his release.

B14C017.summary: Kasyapa asks the emancipated sage how the body dissolves, how the soul moves on to another body, and how it may be freed. The sage explains that harmful habits wear the body down, that heat and wind drive the vital breaths out, and that the soul leaves in pain carrying the record of its deeds. He also describes the heavens and the sufferings of hell that await the soul, which sets up the teaching on rebirth that follows.

scenes.B14C017S01: Kasyapa asks how the body dies and how the soul is freed; the sage explains how harmful habits lead to death, how the soul leaves the body, and what afterlife follows.

shots.B14C017S01H01: Vasudeva says that a Brahmana visitor asks the sage hard questions, and the sage answers them one by one.
shots.B14C017S01H02: Kasyapa asks how the body dissolves, how another is acquired, how the soul is freed from rebirth, and where a bodiless soul's deeds remain.
shots.B14C017S01H03: The Brahmana says that the emancipated sage answered Kasyapa's questions one after another, and he now recites them.
shots.B14C017S01H04: The sage explains how harmful habits and excess heat and wind force the soul out of the body in pain, how it carries its deeds with it, and what heavens and hells await it.

B14C018.summary: The sage explains that a soul's deeds persist through rebirths and bear fruit in each new body, and that the soul enters the womb carrying its past. He lists the conduct of the good, such as gifts, truthfulness, restraint, compassion and reverence for parents and teachers, as the basis of righteousness. He then describes Brahma creating the worlds and the primal matter Pradhana, and says that the wise who see pleasure as impermanent cross the ocean of rebirth.

scenes.B14C018S01: The sage explains how deeds carry over into new bodies, lists the virtues of the good, describes creation, and closes with a teaching on crossing the ocean of rebirth.

shots.B14C018S01H01: The sage explains that deeds bear fruit in each new body and that the soul enters the womb carrying them, lists virtues such as gifts, restraint and compassion, describes Brahma's creation and Pradhana, and says the wise who see the world as impermanent cross the ocean of rebirth.

B14C019.summary: The sage describes the marks of a liberated person: one who is free from attachment, desire, and the pull of opposites, and who sees the soul as separate from the body. He then teaches Yoga, in which the senses are withdrawn and the soul is seen within the body, and the disciple asks about digestion and breath before leaving. Vasudeva concludes that this teaching is secret and hard to grasp, but that practising it for six months brings release.

scenes.B14C019S01: The sage lists the marks of the liberated, teaches Yoga and its meditative method, answers the disciple's questions about the body, and Vasudeva closes by praising the teaching as a rare mystery.

shots.B14C019S01H01: The sage lists the marks of the liberated person, describes the soul seen in deep meditation as a fibre is drawn from a reed, and gives instructions on Yoga and meditation on the body.
shots.B14C019S01H02: The sage recalls the disciple's questions about digestion and breath and his own answers, then says the disciple left after the teaching.
shots.B14C019S01H03: Vasudeva says the teaching is a mystery among the gods that the confused cannot grasp, that liberation is open even to women, Vaisyas and Sudras, and that Yoga practised for six months brings it.

B14C020.summary: Vasudeva tells the story of a learned Brahmana and his wife. She asks what fate awaits her, since her husband has abandoned rites, and he answers that action cannot be wholly escaped and describes the soul's seat in the body. He explains the breaths and an inner fire with seven flames, seven fuels and seven priests, which he presents as an inner sacrifice that creates the world. The story gives a teaching on the inward sacrifice that follows.

scenes.B14C020S01: Vasudeva introduces a Brahmana couple; the wife asks what will become of her, and the husband describes the soul's seat, the breaths, and the seven-flamed inner fire.

shots.B14C020S01H01: Vasudeva tells of a Brahmana who has mastered knowledge, whose wife asks where she will go with him, since he has given up rites; he answers that action cannot be avoided and describes the soul's seat, the breaths, the inner seven-flamed fire, and the sevenfold creation.

B14C021.summary: The Brahmana describes an inner sacrifice with ten priests, ten libations and ten fires, in which the mind serves as the ladle. His wife asks why Word arose after Mind and how breath works in sleep, and he explains that Prana is governed by Apana and that Mind rests on Prana. He then recounts a dispute in which Word yields to Mind, and concludes that the mind is the unmoving part and speech the moving one.

scenes.B14C021S01: The Brahmana describes the inner sacrifice of ten priests and libations, his wife asks about the origin of Word and Mind, and he recounts the old dispute between them.
scenes.B14C021S02: The Brahmana explains how Word moves through the breaths and why Mind is fixed while Word is moving.

shots.B14C021S01H01: The Brahmana describes an inner sacrifice with ten priests, ten libations, ten fires, the mind as ladle, and the knower living in the body, and says that Word arose from the Veda and then Mind.
shots.B14C021S01H02: The wife asks why Word arose after Mind, whether Prana takes refuge in Mind, and what restrains Prana in dreamless sleep.
shots.B14C021S01H03: The Brahmana explains that Apana controls Prana, that the mind depends on Prana, and tells of Word and Mind asking the Soul which is superior, with Mind judged superior and Word yielding.
shots.B14C021S01H04: The Brahmana says he has two minds, one unmoving and one moving, and describes how Word can flow with or without utterance, and how Word, once sinking into Apana, returned to Prana.
shots.B14C021S01H05: The wife asks what Word said long ago when speech could not come out.
shots.B14C021S02H01: The Brahmana explains how Word moves through the breaths from Prana to Apana, Udana, Vyana and Samana, so Mind is the fixed one and Word the moving one.

B14C022.summary: The Brahmana describes seven inner priests, the five senses plus mind and understanding, which cannot perceive one another's qualities, since each senses only its own object. His wife asks why, and he recounts a dispute in which the Mind claims that the senses cannot work without it. The senses reply that the mind relies on them and that pleasure comes only through the objects they grasp, so the mind is not superior.

scenes.B14C022S01: The Brahmana names seven inner priests that cannot perceive one another's qualities; his wife asks why, and he recounts the argument between the senses and the mind.

shots.B14C022S01H01: The Brahmana names seven inner priests, the nose, eye, tongue, skin, ear, mind and understanding, which dwell in subtle space and do not perceive one another.
shots.B14C022S01H02: The wife asks how these priests fail to perceive one another and what their natures are.
shots.B14C022S01H03: The Brahmana explains that each sense perceives only its own object, and introduces an old story of a debate between the senses and the mind.
shots.B14C022S01H04: The Mind claims that the senses cannot work without it, since it is the eternal and foremost element.
shots.B14C022S01H05: The Senses reply that the Mind depends on them, that enjoyment requires their objects, and that rules bind only the weak.

B14C023.summary: The Brahmana names the five life-breaths (Prana, Apana, Udana, Samana and Vyana) as five inner priests and tells how each breath in turn claims to be the foremost, saying that its departure would end all the others. The breaths then argue until Brahma rules that none is superior, that each has its own role and sphere, and that they should live together in harmony. The story teaches that the inner powers are equal partners.

scenes.B14C023S01: The Brahmana introduces the five breaths as inner priests, and their first claim to supremacy is made by Prana.
scenes.B14C023S02: Each breath in turn claims to be foremost, until Brahma says that none is superior and each has its own role.

shots.B14C023S01H01: The Brahmana names Prana, Apana, Udana, Samana and Vyana as the five inner priests.
shots.B14C023S01H02: The wife says she had believed there are seven priests and asks how there can be five.
shots.B14C023S01H03: The Brahmana explains that the breaths arise from one another, and that the good beings asked the Grandsire which of them is foremost.
shots.B14C023S01H04: The Grandsire says the foremost is the one on whose extinction and movement all the breaths depend.
shots.B14C023S01H05: Prana claims to be foremost, since all breaths stop when he stops and start when he moves.
shots.B14C023S02H01: Samana and Udana tell Prana that he is not foremost, since Apana is under his control, and Prana moves on.
shots.B14C023S02H02: Apana makes the same claim to be foremost, based on the same reasoning.
shots.B14C023S02H03: Vyana, disputing Apana, claims the same supremacy.
shots.B14C023S02H04: The others reject Vyana's claim, Samana makes his own claim, and Udana claims the same.
shots.B14C023S02H05: Brahma tells the breaths that none is superior, that each has its own attributes and sphere, and asks them to uphold one another.

B14C024.summary: Narada explains to the Rishi Devamata how a creature's life-breaths arise and come in pairs, moving across, upward and downward, from wish, sensation and the union of seed and blood. He ties the breaths to fire and to the pairs of opposites, and ends by saying that the calm breath, Vyana, reaches the eternal Brahman. The teaching presents the breaths as the first steps toward that calm.

scenes.B14C024S01: Devamata asks Narada which breath arises first in a new creature; Narada explains the breaths' pairing and their link to fire, desire and calm.

shots.B14C024S01H01: The Brahmana introduces the old discourse between Narada and the Rishi Devamata.
shots.B14C024S01H02: Devamata asks which life-breath comes first in a newborn creature.
shots.B14C024S01H03: Narada says what comes first is what is separate from the creature, and that the breaths work in pairs moving across, upward and downward.
shots.B14C024S01H04: Devamata asks which breath produces a creature and asks for the pairs.
shots.B14C024S01H05: Narada traces the breaths to wish, sensation, seed and blood, links them to fire, the pairs of opposites, and calm, which is Brahman.

B14C025.summary: The Brahmana describes a four-part inner sacrifice in which the agent, the instrument, the action and release are the four priests of the universe. He says that the breaths are the chants and rites of an inner sacrifice of Yoga, that renunciation is the fee, and that Narayana is the soul of all. The chapter widens the inner-sacrifice teaching into a full ritual picture.

scenes.B14C025S01: The Brahmana presents the four-part inner sacrifice, with the breaths as its chants and renunciation as its fee, and closes by naming Narayana as the soul of all.

shots.B14C025S01H01: The Brahmana describes a four-part sacrifice of agent, instrument, action and release, lists the senses and their objects as causes, and says the breaths and renunciation serve as the inner rites and fee, closing with the praise of Narayana.

B14C026.summary: The Brahmana says there is one ruler, one preceptor, one kinsman, one dispeller and one enemy, and each of them lives in the heart. He tells a story in which the Lord of creatures answers the gods, snakes, sages, Asuras and Danavas with the single word Om, and each group takes a different path. He ends by describing the brahmacharin who lives in Brahman, teaching that the inner guide shapes a person's conduct.

scenes.B14C026S01: The Brahmana teaches that one inner ruler, preceptor and enemy each dwell in the heart; the Lord of creatures answers the beings with the word Om, and each group takes a different disposition.

shots.B14C026S01H01: The Brahmana teaches that one inner ruler, preceptor, kinsman, dispeller and enemy dwell in the heart, tells how the Lord of creatures answers all beings with Om and each group takes a different disposition, and describes the brahmacharin who lives in Brahman.

B14C027.summary: The Brahmana describes the world as a dangerous forest full of desires, grief and passions, and says that he has crossed it into a greater forest of Brahman. His wife asks what that forest is like, and he describes its sevenfold trees, fruits, guests, hermitages and streams, with intelligence as the tree and liberation as the fruit. The passage is a metaphor for the inner path toward Brahman.

scenes.B14C027S01: The Brahmana describes crossing the dangerous worldly forest and entering the forest of Brahman; his wife asks about it, and he describes its trees, fruits, rivers and the sages who dwell there.

shots.B14C027S01H01: The Brahmana says he has crossed the dangerous worldly forest and entered the wider forest of Brahman.
shots.B14C027S01H02: His wife asks where that forest is and what its trees, rivers and hills are like.
shots.B14C027S01H03: The Brahmana describes the forest's sevenfold trees, fruits, guests and hermitages, its inner fire of the senses, intelligence as its tree and liberation as its fruit, and the streams that lead the sages to Brahman.

B14C028.summary: The Brahmana says that he is free of desire and aversion, which belong to Nature, and offers as an illustration a debate between a Yati, an ascetic who opposes harm, and an Adhwaryu, a priest who is about to sacrifice a goat. The Yati argues that taking life is wrong and that the soul cannot be destroyed, and the Adhwaryu admits the force of the argument. The Brahmana concludes that the priest completed the sacrifice free of delusion, which shows how the wise live.

scenes.B14C028S01: The Brahmana describes his detachment and tells of the Yati's protest against the goat sacrifice, the priest's defence, and the Yati's view that the soul is beyond destruction.
scenes.B14C028S02: The Brahmana concludes that the Yati fell silent and the priest completed the sacrifice free of delusion.

shots.B14C028S01H01: The Brahmana says he is free of desire and aversion, and begins the tale of the Yati who objects to the goat sacrifice and the Adhwaryu who defends it.
shots.B14C028S01H02: The Yati says the goat's life-breaths should be returned, asks for the consent of its kin, and says that non-violence is the foremost duty.
shots.B14C028S01H03: The Adhwaryu says that all things have life and that living is impossible without some slaughter.
shots.B14C028S01H04: The Yati says the soul has an indestructible part, that the body is not the soul, and that the freed person has no fear.
shots.B14C028S01H05: The Adhwaryu thanks the Yati, says he will follow the wise, and claims that he is not at fault in performing the rite with mantras.
shots.B14C028S02H01: The Brahmana says that the Yati fell silent, the priest finished the sacrifice without delusion, and the wise live by this understanding.

B14C029.summary: The Brahmana tells of Kartaviryarjuna, the thousand-armed king, who angers the ocean by shooting arrows into it. He challenges anyone to match him, and the ocean sends him to Rama, the son of Jamadagni. Rama kills the king in battle, and then turns against the Kshatriyas over and over until a heavenly voice and his ancestors order him to stop, since a Brahmana should not slay kings.

scenes.B14C029S01: The Brahmana tells of Kartaviryarjuna shooting at the ocean; the ocean sends him to Rama, Rama kills the king, destroys the Kshatriyas, and is told by heaven and his ancestors to stop.

shots.B14C029S01H01: The Brahmana introduces Kartaviryarjuna, the thousand-armed king who conquers the earth, and tells how he shoots hundreds of arrows at the ocean, which begs him to stop.
shots.B14C029S01H02: Arjuna asks the ocean to name any archer equal to him in battle.
shots.B14C029S01H03: The ocean points him to Rama, the son of Jamadagni, whom Arjuna attacks and who kills him with an axe; Rama then slaughters Kshatriyas, a heavenly voice and his ancestors tell him to stop, and he refuses until they tell him a Brahmana should not slay kings.

B14C030.summary: The Pitris tell Rama the story of the royal sage Alarka, who conquered the earth and then turned to the inner conquest of the senses. He aims arrows at the mind, nose, tongue, skin, ear, eye and understanding, and each in turn warns him the arrows will only harm him. He then finds that Yoga alone wins, slays the senses in concentration, and sings that nothing is happier than Yoga. The Pitris urge Rama to stop killing Kshatriyas and take up penance, and he does so and succeeds.

scenes.B14C030S01: The Pitris introduce Alarka, who first aims arrows at the mind and then at the nose, which each reply that the arrows cannot harm them.
scenes.B14C030S02: Alarka aims at the tongue, the skin, and the ear; each sense answers that his arrows will only pierce his own vital parts.
scenes.B14C030S03: Alarka aims at the eye and then at the understanding; each again warns him that his arrows are useless.
scenes.B14C030S04: Alarka turns to Yoga and slays the senses through concentration; the Pitris tell Rama to stop killing Kshatriyas and take up penance, which he does.

shots.B14C030S01H01: The Pitris tell of the royal sage Alarka, who conquered the earth and then turned his mind to the subtle inner life.
shots.B14C030S01H02: Alarka says he has conquered his mind and resolves to aim arrows at it.
shots.B14C030S01H03: The mind replies that the arrows will only pierce Alarka's own vital parts and tells him to find other weapons.
shots.B14C030S01H04: Alarka says the nose craves perfumes and resolves to aim arrows at it.
shots.B14C030S01H05: The nose replies that the arrows will only harm Alarka himself.
shots.B14C030S02H01: Alarka says the tongue craves savoury tastes and resolves to shoot at it.
shots.B14C030S02H02: The tongue replies that the arrows will only pierce Alarka.
shots.B14C030S02H03: Alarka says the skin craves touch and resolves to tear it with feathered arrows.
shots.B14C030S02H04: The skin replies that the arrows would only pierce Alarka's vital parts.
shots.B14C030S02H05: Alarka says the ear craves sounds and resolves to shoot at it.
shots.B14C030S03H01: The ear replies that the arrows would only harm Alarka.
shots.B14C030S03H02: Alarka says the eye craves colours.
shots.B14C030S03H03: Alarka resolves to destroy the eye with sharp arrows.
shots.B14C030S03H04: The eye replies that the arrows would only pierce Alarka's own vital parts.
shots.B14C030S03H05: Alarka says the understanding forms many judgements and resolves to shoot at it.
shots.B14C030S04H01: The understanding replies that the arrows would only pierce Alarka's vital parts.
shots.B14C030S04H02: Alarka, unable to find weapons against the senses, turns to concentrated Yoga, slays the senses with one arrow, and sings that Yoga is the highest happiness; the grandsires tell Rama to stop killing Kshatriyas and take up penance, which he does and succeeds.

B14C031.summary: The Brahmana names the three sets of three qualities (goodness, passion and darkness) as the threefold foes within, and says a steady man conquers them with his senses under control. He then quotes King Amvarisha, who had conquered many faults but not craving, which keeps the living bound to rebirth. Amvarisha concludes that the true sovereignty is rule over the soul.

scenes.B14C031S01: The Brahmana names the inner foes and the qualities linked to each; he then quotes King Amvarisha, who names craving as the greatest foe and says the soul is the true king.

shots.B14C031S01H01: The Brahmana names the three sets of three qualities as inner foes, then quotes King Amvarisha, who says craving remains the greatest foe he failed to conquer and that the soul alone is the true king.

B14C032.summary: The Brahmana recounts how King Janaka, angry at a guilty Brahmana, orders him banished, and the Brahmana asks where he may go. Janaka is struck speechless, then says he cannot find anything that is truly his, not on earth, in Mithila or among his children. He explains that he is indifferent to the pleasures of the senses, so the world is his in one sense and nothing in another. The Brahmana then reveals that he is Dharma, who came to test the king, and praises Janaka's understanding.

scenes.B14C032S01: Janaka threatens to banish a Brahmana, who asks where he may go; the king is struck silent, then explains his detachment, and the Brahmana reveals he is Dharma.

shots.B14C032S01H01: The Brahmana recounts how King Janaka orders a guilty Brahmana banished, and how the Brahmana, asking where he may go, leaves the king stunned into silence.
shots.B14C032S01H02: Janaka says he cannot find any part of his kingdom, not on earth, in Mithila or among his children, and that he regards everything as both his and not his.
shots.B14C032S01H03: The Brahmana asks what understanding has freed Janaka from the idea of mine.
shots.B14C032S01H04: Janaka says all things are impermanent, that he does not crave the pleasures of the senses, and that his acts serve the gods and ancestors; the Brahmana then reveals he is Dharma and praises the king.

B14C033.summary: The Brahmana tells his wife that he is a learned, liberated man who lives as a householder and as a forest recluse, and that the knowledge of his identity with the universe is his wealth. He says there is one path for Brahmanas that leads to the same goal whatever their station, and that actions bind the body but understanding carries a person along the path. He reassures his wife that she need not fear the world to come, since she will reach his soul.

scenes.B14C033S01: The Brahmana presents himself as a liberated man of many roles, says knowledge is his wealth, describes the one path, and reassures his wife.

shots.B14C033S01H01: The Brahmana describes his liberated life and his knowledge of the universe, explains that there is one path for all Brahmanas, and tells his wife she need not fear the world to come.

B14C034.summary: The Brahmana's wife asks how knowledge can be gained, and her husband answers with the image of two fire-sticks: devotion to Brahman as the lower stick and the teacher as the upper, rubbed by austerity and study to kindle the fire of knowledge. The Kshetrajna, the knower of the field, is without qualities, but can be grasped by an understanding cleansed through action. When the wife grasps this, she moves beyond the knower. Arjuna then asks Krishna where that Brahmana and his wife are, and Krishna replies that he himself is the Kshetrajna.

scenes.B14C034S01: The Brahmana's wife asks how knowledge is gained; the Brahmana describes the fire-sticks of knowledge and the way to perceive the Kshetrajna, and she reaches beyond it.
scenes.B14C034S02: Arjuna asks where the Brahmana and his wife are; Krishna says that the mind is the Brahmana, the understanding is the wife, and that he is the Kshetrajna.

shots.B14C034S01H01: The wife asks why this knowledge is hard to grasp, and asks how it can be gained.
shots.B14C034S01H02: The Brahmana describes devotion to Brahman as the lower fire-stick, the teacher as the upper, and study and austerity as the friction that produces the fire of knowledge.
shots.B14C034S01H03: The wife asks how the Kshetrajna, which is called a symbol of Brahman, can be grasped.
shots.B14C034S01H04: The Brahmana says the Kshetrajna has no qualities, can be perceived by a cleansed understanding as bees find flowers, and that practice leads to what lies above it.
shots.B14C034S01H05: The holy one continues the frame of the story: once the Kshetrajna is destroyed in her understanding, the wife becomes beyond the Kshetrajna through her knowledge.
shots.B14C034S02H01: Arjuna asks where the Brahmana and his wife are, by whom such success was won.
shots.B14C034S02H02: Krishna says that his mind is the Brahmana, his understanding is the Brahmana's wife, and he himself is the Kshetrajna.

B14C035.summary: Arjuna asks Krishna to explain Brahma, the highest object of knowledge. Krishna recounts a dialogue in which a devoted disciple asks his preceptor what the highest good is, and the preceptor answers that knowledge is the highest goal and renunciation the best penance. The preceptor then tells how the great sages went to Brahma to ask the same questions, which leads into Brahma's teaching on truth, the stages of life and the elements.

scenes.B14C035S01: Arjuna asks to hear about Brahma; Krishna introduces a preceptor-disciple dialogue, in which the disciple asks questions and the preceptor answers that knowledge and renunciation are the highest, and tells how sages approached Brahma with the same questions.
scenes.B14C035S02: Brahma answers the sages' questions, teaching that all things come from Truth, that the stages of life form the path, and that understanding the elements frees a person from sin.

shots.B14C035S01H01: Arjuna asks Krishna to expound Brahma, the highest object of knowledge.
shots.B14C035S01H02: Krishna introduces an old dialogue in which a devoted disciple asks his preceptor what the highest good is.
shots.B14C035S01H03: The disciple asks a series of questions about where he is, the origin of creatures, what truth is, what sin and happiness are, and asks for release from worldly life.
shots.B14C035S01H04: Krishna says the preceptor, pleased with the disciple's service and humility, answered all his questions.
shots.B14C035S01H05: The preceptor says the teaching is from Brahma, that knowledge is the highest object and renunciation the best penance, and tells how the great sages asked Brahma about the highest good, starting with the question of how a good man should act.
shots.B14C035S02H01: Brahma answers that all creatures arise from Truth, that the four stages of life form a path, that the twenty-four elements, with one more, must be understood, and that whoever understands them is freed from sin.

B14C036.summary: Brahma describes the quality of Darkness, which binds the body's city of nine gates and its three inner ducts, and lists the faults it brings, such as delusion, sloth, anger and hostility. People ruled by Darkness sink into lower births, such as animals, insects or the afflicted, but those born in such states can rise again through the rites of Brahmanas. The chapter closes by naming the five great afflictions and urging that Darkness be understood and left behind.

scenes.B14C036S01: Brahma describes the body as a city governed by the three qualities, lists the faults of Darkness and their consequences, and shows how those ruled by it can rise again.

shots.B14C036S01H01: Brahma describes the body as a city ruled by the three qualities, lists the faults of Darkness, shows the lower births it leads to, explains how such beings may rise, and urges that Darkness be understood and left behind.

B14C037.summary: Brahma turns to the quality of Passion, which drives people to action, desire, pride, quarrel and worldly ambition. He lists many forms of this quality, from war and trade to ritual and charity, and says that people caught in it seek pleasure and reward in this world and the next. Understanding these qualities frees a person from their hold.

scenes.B14C037S01: Brahma lists the many forms of the quality of Passion, describes the people it drives, and says that understanding it frees a person from it.

shots.B14C037S01H01: Brahma lists the qualities of Passion, from desire and pride to trade and ritual, describes the people it drives toward pleasure and reward, and says that understanding these qualities frees one from them.

B14C038.summary: Brahma describes the quality of Goodness, which brings joy, truth, forgiveness, courage, and freedom from anger, malice and the sense of mine. Those who practise it, free from egoism and expectation and treating all with an equal eye, rise upward and gain the power to enjoy whatever they desire without being attached to it. Understanding these qualities is the path to such a state.

scenes.B14C038S01: Brahma describes the qualities of Goodness, the virtues of those who practise it, and their rise to heaven and freedom from attachment.

shots.B14C038S01H01: Brahma describes the qualities of Goodness, such as joy, truth, forgiveness and freedom from ego, the rising path of the good, and their enjoyment of what they desire without attachment.

B14C039.summary: Brahma explains that the three qualities cannot be fully separated, and that one or another predominates in each creature, with Darkness strongest in the lower creatures, Passion in the middle, and Goodness in the higher. These qualities are said to govern the castes, the times of day, the seasons and the elements of the body, and all of them act in the unmanifest. Those who understand the qualities and their workings are freed from the body and gain lasting happiness.

scenes.B14C039S01: Brahma explains that the three qualities are always combined, shows how each dominates in different creatures and castes, and says that the wise who understand them gain freedom.

shots.B14C039S01H01: Brahma explains that the three qualities always act together, that one dominates in each creature, that they are linked to castes and to many things in the world, and that understanding them frees one from the body.

B14C040.summary: Brahma says that from the unmanifest first arose Mahat, the Great Soul, which is the source of all the qualities and the first creation. He lists its many names and describes it as the Being dwelling in the heart of all things. Those who understand this Great Soul are freed from delusion and live above the understanding.

scenes.B14C040S01: Brahma names the Great Soul as the first creation from the unmanifest, describes its nature, and says that knowing it frees one from delusion.

shots.B14C040S01H01: Brahma says that the Great Soul, Mahat, arose first from the unmanifest, lists its names, describes the Being in every heart, and says the one who knows it is freed from delusion.

B14C041.summary: Brahma says that the Great Soul gives rise to Egoism, which he calls the second creation, from which all beings come and which feels the thought I am all this. Those who are content with knowledge of the self, and who have won success through study and sacrifice, enjoy the eternal world. The passage links the self-sense to the enjoyment of the qualities and to the creation of the worlds.

scenes.B14C041S01: Brahma says that the Great Soul gives rise to Egoism, the second creation, which is the source of beings and feels that it is all this, and that consciousness of the self leads to enjoyment of the qualities.

shots.B14C041S01H01: Brahma says that Egoism arises from the Great Soul as the second creation, is the source of all creatures, and that the sages who are content with knowledge of the self reach the eternal world.

B14C042.summary: Brahma explains how the five great elements arise from Egoism and how creation and dissolution run in reverse order. He lists the five life-breaths and the eleven organs, which include the senses, the organs of action and the mind, and assigns each a presiding deity, as well as the four modes of birth. He then describes the path of renunciation in which the senses are withdrawn and the self is seen in all beings, and ends by praising the Highest that is seen this way.

scenes.B14C042S01: Brahma covers the elements, the breaths and organs with their deities, the four kinds of birth, and the inward path of renunciation by which the self is seen in all beings.

shots.B14C042S01H01: Brahma describes the five elements arising from Egoism, the dissolution of creation in reverse order, the breaths and organs with their deities, the four kinds of birth, the withdrawal of the senses, and the Highest seen in all creatures.

B14C043.summary: Brahma names the foremost of each class of beings and things, such as the royal Kshatriya among men, the elephant among vehicles, and Vishnu and Shiva among the gods, and he says that kings must protect the Brahmanas and good men. He then teaches non-injury as the highest duty and gives the characteristic of each element, sense and mental faculty, along with the powers that govern them. He concludes that the Kshetrajna, the knower of the field, is pure knowledge and is not seized by any symbol.

scenes.B14C043S01: Brahma names the foremost of each class of things, teaches that kings must protect good men, gives the marks of the elements and senses, and describes the Kshetrajna as pure knowledge.

shots.B14C043S01H01: Brahma names the foremost of each class of beings and things, urges kings to protect the Brahmanas and good men, sets out non-injury as the highest duty, gives the marks of each sense and element and their governing powers, and describes the Kshetrajna as pure knowledge that is not seized by symbols.

B14C044.summary: Brahma lists the first of many things, including the day, Om among the Vedas, gold among precious things, the householder's mode of life, Meru among mountains and the Ganga among rivers. He then teaches that all things created end in destruction and that only knowledge has no end. A person who is calm, restrained, free of possession and self-regard is released from sin by pure knowledge.

scenes.B14C044S01: Brahma names the first of many things and their order, teaches that all things end in destruction, and says that knowledge alone has no end.

shots.B14C044S01H01: Brahma lists the first of many things, from day and the sun to the householder's life and the Ganga, says that all things created end in destruction while knowledge has no end, and concludes that pure knowledge frees one from sin.

B14C045.summary: Brahma describes the wheel of life, which turns through grief, passion and time, with understanding as its strength, the mind as its hub and the senses as its spokes. One who understands its motion and stopping is free from delusion and from sin. Brahma then sets out the rules for the householder, who supports the other three stages of life, including the five sacrifices, teaching and receiving gifts from the pure, and says that faithful observance of these duties wins heaven.

scenes.B14C045S01: Brahma describes the wheel of life and says it is freed by understanding its motion; he then sets out the householder's duties, the six acts, and the reward of heaven.

shots.B14C045S01H01: Brahma describes the wheel of life, says that understanding its motion frees one from delusion, lays out the householder's duties and six acts, and says that faithful observance of these duties wins heaven.

B14C046.summary: Brahma lays out a graded way of life: the student who serves his teacher, the forest dweller who gives up his village, and the wandering renouncer who owns nothing, begs for his food and keeps eight vows of harmlessness, truth, restraint and freedom from backbiting. He describes the self as beyond the senses and the qualities, and says that one who knows it escapes death. The chapter ends with the mind fixed on that self at the time of death, and release follows.

scenes.B14C046S01: Brahma describes the duties of the student, the forest dweller and the wandering renunciant, the eight vows, and the inner self that brings release at death.

shots.B14C046S01H01: Brahma describes the duties of the student, the forest dweller and the wandering renunciant in detail, including diet, dress, vows, begging, freedom from possessions, and the inner self that brings release at death.

B14C047.summary: Brahma says that renunciation is the best penance and that knowledge is the highest, and he describes Brahman as beyond opposites and qualities. He uses the image of an eternal tree of Brahman, cut down with the sword of knowledge, and of two birds, one unintelligent and one intelligent. The one who understands the field and transcends the qualities is freed from every sin.

scenes.B14C047S01: Brahma calls renunciation the best penance and knowledge the highest, uses the image of the eternal tree and the two birds, and says that understanding the field frees one from sin.

shots.B14C047S01H01: Brahma calls renunciation the best penance, describes Brahman as beyond the opposites and the qualities, uses the tree and two birds as images, and says that one who understands the field and transcends the qualities is freed from sin.

B14C048.summary: Brahma explains that different thinkers regard Brahman as a tree, a forest, the unmanifest, or beyond all distress, and that a moment of inner peace, or breath control, leads to immortality. He ties Purusha, the self, to the quality of Goodness and says that some who claim that Nature and the self are one are mistaken, since they differ, like a fish and the water it lives in. The learned sages, still uncertain, then ask the Grandsire again, as the preceptor reports.

scenes.B14C048S01: Brahma describes the many views of Brahman, links the self to Goodness, and says the self and Nature differ; the sages still have doubts and question the Grandsire again.

shots.B14C048S01H01: Brahma describes Brahman as a tree, a forest, the unmanifest and beyond distress, says that inner peace and breath control lead to immortality, ties the self to Goodness, and says that the self and Nature are distinct, though they are joined like a fish in water.
shots.B14C048S01H02: The preceptor says that the Brahmanas were still in doubt and once more questioned the Grandsire.

B14C049.summary: The Rishis complain that the many contradictory teachings on duty leave them confused, with some saying the soul survives death and others that it does not, and different people praising action, tranquillity, sacrifice, knowledge or renunciation. They ask Brahma to say which duty is most worthy and what links the knower of the field with Nature. Brahma prepares to answer their questions, which opens the next stage of the teaching.

scenes.B14C049S01: The Rishis list the contradictory views on duty and ask Brahma which duty is most worthy and how the knower of the field is linked to Nature; Brahma answers them.

shots.B14C049S01H01: The Rishis say that teachings on duty contradict one another, list the many rival views, and ask Brahma which duty is most worthy and how the knower of the field is linked to Nature; the Creator then prepares to answer.

B14C050.summary: Brahma explains that harmlessness is the highest duty and that pure knowledge frees one from sin. He sets out the relation between the knower, Purusha, who enjoys, and Nature, the enjoyed, which is like a lotus leaf and water, and traces Nature's order from the unmanifest through Mahat, Egoism and the five elements. Each element is given its qualities in detail, such as the ten kinds of smell and the twelve kinds of colour, and the chapter ends by placing Purusha above all of these as the Unfading Soul.

scenes.B14C050S01: Brahma teaches harmlessness and knowledge, explains the knower and Nature as enjoyer and enjoyed, lists the qualities of the five elements, and places Purusha above them all.

shots.B14C050S01H01: Brahma teaches that harmlessness is the highest duty and knowledge the highest happiness, explains the knower and Nature, gives their order and the qualities of the elements, and places the soul above all of them.

B14C051.summary: Brahma says that the mind governs the senses and the elements, and describes the body as a chariot driven by the mind, with understanding as reins. He teaches that penance accomplishes all things, that attachment is death and detachment eternal, and that understanding the immortal self brings tranquillity. Vasudeva then reveals that he was the preceptor and Arjuna's mind the pupil, urges Arjuna to practise the teaching, and asks leave to visit his father. Arjuna agrees to go to the elephant-named city to meet Yudhishthira and report Krishna's intention.

scenes.B14C051S01: Brahma describes the mind's rule over the elements, the chariot image, the power of penance, and the immortal self; the sages act on his words, and Vasudeva reveals he was the preceptor and asks leave to visit his father.
scenes.B14C051S02: Arjuna agrees to go to the elephant-named city, meet Yudhishthira and inform him of Krishna's plan to depart.

shots.B14C051S01H01: Brahma says that the mind rules the elements and that the body is a chariot driven by the mind, with penance achieving all things, attachment as death, and the immortal self as the goal.
shots.B14C051S01H02: The preceptor says the sages who followed Brahma's teaching attained many regions of happiness, and urges the hearer to do likewise.
shots.B14C051S01H03: Vasudeva says that the pupil followed the teaching and attained emancipation, having done what he should.
shots.B14C051S01H04: Arjuna asks who the Brahmana and the pupil were.
shots.B14C051S01H05: Vasudeva says that he is the preceptor and Arjuna's mind the pupil, urges Arjuna to practise the teaching, and asks leave to visit his father.
shots.B14C051S02H01: Vaisampayana reports that Arjuna answers Krishna, saying they will go to the elephant-named city, meet Yudhishthira and tell him of Krishna's intention to leave.

B14C052.summary: Krishna and Arjuna drive to the city named after the elephant, where Arjuna praises Krishna as the soul of the universe who won the war for the Pandavas. They are received by Dhritarashtra and the family, and in the morning they tell Yudhishthira that Krishna wishes to visit his kin in Dvaraka. Yudhishthira grants leave and offers gems and wealth, and Krishna sets out with his kinsmen and attendants, so the bond between the two heroes is marked by a formal parting.

scenes.B14C052S01: Krishna and Arjuna arrive at Hastinapura, visit the family, and the next morning Arjuna asks Yudhishthira's leave for Krishna to go to Dvaraka, which is granted with gifts.
scenes.B14C052S02: Yudhishthira gives Krishna leave to depart; Krishna takes leave of Kunti and sets out with his company toward the city of the Anarttas.

shots.B14C052S01H01: Krishna orders his car yoked, the party sets out for the elephant-named city, and Arjuna praises Krishna as the soul of the universe who won the war, and the two arrive at the palace, meet Dhritarashtra and the family, and spend the night.
shots.B14C052S01H02: Yudhishthira asks the two heroes what they want to say to him.
shots.B14C052S01H03: Arjuna asks Yudhishthira to let Krishna visit his father in the city of the Anarttas, since he has been away a long time.
shots.B14C052S01H04: Yudhishthira grants leave, asks Krishna to see his uncles and the family in Dvaraka, to return for the horse sacrifice, and to take gems and wealth.
shots.B14C052S01H05: Krishna is about to respond to Yudhishthira.
shots.B14C052S02H01: Krishna says all the wealth is Yudhishthira's, takes leave of Kunti and the family, and sets out with his sister Subhadra, Satyaki, Bhima and others, toward the city of the Anarttas.

B14C053.summary: On the road home, Krishna meets the ascetic Utanka in a dry desert and asks about the Kuru war. Krishna explains that he tried to make peace, but that fate and the Kauravas' own folly led to the total destruction of their side, with only the five Pandavas left. Utanka, angry that Krishna did not stop the war, threatens a curse, and Krishna pleads that the ascetic listen to him first and not lose the penance he has built up.

scenes.B14C053S01: Krishna meets Utanka in the desert; Utanka asks about peace with the Kurus, Krishna explains the war's outcome, and Utanka threatens a curse, which Krishna answers with a plea.

shots.B14C053S01H01: Krishna rides home, marks of divine favour attend him, and in a desert he meets the ascetic Utanka, who asks whether he has made peace between the Kurus and Pandavas and whether the kin will live in harmony.
shots.B14C053S01H02: Krishna says he tried hard to make peace, but the Kauravas refused advice and were destroyed, leaving only the five Pandavas alive.
shots.B14C053S01H03: Utanka, angered, says that Krishna should have forced the Kauravas to keep the peace and threatens him with a curse.
shots.B14C053S01H04: Krishna asks Utanka to hear his teaching on the self before cursing him, and says he does not want the ascetic's penance destroyed.

B14C054.summary: Utanka asks Krishna to teach him the Adhyatma, the teaching on the self. Krishna declares that the three qualities, the gods, the Vedas, the sacrifices and Dharma all rest on him, that he takes many forms to uphold righteousness, and that the Kauravas were destroyed by their own wrongdoing and the power of Time. He concludes that the Pandavas have won great fame. The teaching explains to Utanka why Krishna did not prevent the war.

scenes.B14C054S01: Utanka asks for the teaching; Krishna says he is the source of all beings and qualities, takes many forms to protect righteousness, and explains that the Kauravas fell through their own wrong.

shots.B14C054S01H01: Utanka asks Krishna to teach him the faultless Adhyatma, so that he can decide whether to bless or curse Krishna.
shots.B14C054S01H02: Krishna declares that all the qualities, beings, Vedas, sacrifices and Dharma come from him, that he takes birth in many forms to uphold righteousness, and that the Kauravas were destroyed for their unrighteousness while the Pandavas gained fame.

B14C055.summary: Utanka is moved by Krishna's teaching and says his anger has gone, asking to see Krishna's sovereign form. Krishna shows him a vast cosmic form, which overwhelms Utanka, who then asks to see the human form again. Krishna grants a boon: whenever Utanka thirsts in the desert, he may call on him. Later, Utanka is refused a proffered water by a hunter, who turns out to be Indra in disguise, offering nectar. Krishna promises that clouds will bring water to the desert, which become known as the Utanka-clouds.

scenes.B14C055S01: Utanka praises Krishna and asks for a vision of his form; Krishna shows his cosmic form, grants a boon, and in the desert Utanka refuses water from a hunter; Krishna explains that the hunter was Indra with nectar, and promises the Utanka-clouds.

shots.B14C055S01H01: Utanka says that his anger is gone, that he now knows Krishna as creator of the universe, and asks to see Krishna's sovereign form.
shots.B14C055S01H02: Vaisampayana describes Krishna showing Utanka the vast form of Vishnu, with many faces and arms, blazing like a thousand suns, filling all space.
shots.B14C055S01H03: Utanka praises the cosmic form, which covers the earth, sky and quarters, and asks to see the human form again.
shots.B14C055S01H04: Vaisampayana reports that Krishna invites Utanka to ask for a boon, and Utanka asks for water whenever he needs it in the desert, and Krishna agrees to grant it.
shots.B14C055S01H05: Utanka, thirsty, calls on Krishna in the desert, meets a hunter who offers water; Utanka refuses in anger. Krishna explains that the hunter was Indra, that Indra had been asked to give nectar, and promises the clouds that will bring water to the desert.

B14C056.summary: Janamejaya asks what penance gave Utanka the nerve to threaten Vishnu. Vaisampayana explains that Utanka served his teacher Gautama with unmatched devotion, so Gautama would not let him leave, and in old age Utanka breaks down in tears after his load of wood breaks and his white hair falls. Gautama rewards him with his daughter in marriage and restores his youth, and then Utanka, at the request of Ahalya, the teacher's wife, sets out to fetch the celestial ear-rings of Saudasa's queen. Gautama warns that the cursed king Saudasa may kill him, and Utanka meets the king in the forest.

scenes.B14C056S01: Utanka's devotion to Gautama, his old age and tears, Gautama's kindness and offer of his daughter, and Utanka's gratitude.
scenes.B14C056S02: Utanka restored to youth marries Gautama's daughter, Ahalya asks him to fetch the ear-rings of Saudasa's queen, Gautama warns of danger, and Utanka meets Saudasa in the forest.

shots.B14C056S01H01: Janamejaya asks what penances made Utanka willing to curse Vishnu.
shots.B14C056S01H02: Vaisampayana describes Utanka's devotion to his teacher Gautama, who would not let him leave, and his old age, which Utanka did not notice until he dropped his load of wood and wept at the sight of a white lock of hair.
shots.B14C056S01H03: Utanka tells Gautama he has served him for a hundred years without rest and asks to be allowed to go.
shots.B14C056S01H04: Gautama says he did not notice the years passing and gives Utanka leave to go.
shots.B14C056S01H05: Utanka asks what fee he should bring his teacher before leaving.
shots.B14C056S02H01: Gautama says that pleasing the teacher is the fee, and offers his daughter in marriage if Utanka becomes a youth; Utanka is made young and marries her, then asks Ahalya what gift he may bring.
shots.B14C056S02H02: Ahalya says she is satisfied and tells him to go.
shots.B14C056S02H03: Utanka asks again for a command he can fulfil for her.
shots.B14C056S02H04: Ahalya asks him to bring the celestial ear-rings of Saudasa's queen; Utanka sets out, and Gautama warns that the cursed king may kill him.
shots.B14C056S02H05: Ahalya says she did not know the danger and asks that Utanka be spared; Gautama agrees, and Utanka meets Saudasa in a deserted forest.

B14C057.summary: Utanka meets Saudasa, now a man-eater under a curse, who is about to take food and claims the right to eat him. Utanka asks for the queen's ear-rings for his teacher's wife, and Saudasa replies that they belong to his wife and sends him to her. The queen Madayanti demands a sign from her husband, and describes the ear-rings' wonderful powers before she will hand them over.

scenes.B14C057S01: Saudasa, a man-eater under a curse, prepares to eat Utanka, who pleads that he is on his teacher's errand and promises to return; Saudasa asks what he seeks.
scenes.B14C057S02: Utanka asks for the ear-rings; Saudasa sends him to his queen, and Utanka insists on the request.
scenes.B14C057S03: Saudasa sends Utanka to Madayanti, who asks for a sign from her husband and describes the ear-rings' powers.

shots.B14C057S01H01: Vaisampayana describes Utanka undisturbed by the sight of the frightful king, and Saudasa greeting him as a meal at the sixth hour.
shots.B14C057S01H02: Utanka says he is on his teacher's business and that one should not harm a person engaged in such a task.
shots.B14C057S01H03: Saudasa says he is hungry and cannot let Utanka go.
shots.B14C057S01H04: Utanka proposes a compact: he will go do his errand and return to be eaten; he asks for what he seeks, since Saudasa is a generous giver.
shots.B14C057S01H05: Saudasa asks Utanka to name the object he seeks.
shots.B14C057S02H01: Utanka asks Saudasa for the jewelled ear-rings worn by his queen.
shots.B14C057S02H02: Saudasa says the ear-rings belong to his wife and asks Utanka to ask for something else.
shots.B14C057S02H03: Utanka says Saudasa should not use this pretext and should give the ear-rings truthfully.
shots.B14C057S02H04: Saudasa tells Utanka to go to the queen and ask for them in his name.
shots.B14C057S02H05: Utanka asks why Saudasa will not go himself.
shots.B14C057S03H01: Saudasa says Utanka will find the queen near a fountain, since he himself cannot leave at the sixth hour.
shots.B14C057S03H02: Utanka asks Madayanti for the ear-rings; she demands a sign from her husband and describes the ear-rings' powers to produce gold, protect the wearer and fit any size.

B14C058.summary: Saudasa gives Utanka a sign, and Madayanti hands over the ear-rings, after which Saudasa explains that a king hostile to Brahmanas cannot prosper and asks Utanka to keep his promise. Utanka sets out, ties the ear-rings in his deer-skin, and hangs it on a tree while he picks fruit; the fruit knocks the knot loose, and a Naga takes the ear-rings into an anthill. Utanka digs with his staff for thirty-five days until Indra appears in disguise and warns him, and when Utanka insists, Indra opens the way to the Naga world. A fire-steed fills the Naga realm with smoke, the Nagas return the ear-rings with honour, and Utanka delivers them to Ahalya.

scenes.B14C058S01: Saudasa gives a sign, Madayanti gives the ear-rings, and Saudasa explains his reasons and reminds Utanka of his promise.
scenes.B14C058S02: Utanka asks whether to return to the cannibal king, Saudasa advises him not to, and the ear-rings are lost to a Naga in the forest.
scenes.B14C058S03: Indra opens the way to the Naga world, a fire-steed fills it with smoke, the Nagas return the ear-rings, and Utanka brings them to Ahalya.

shots.B14C058S01H01: Utanka asks Saudasa for a sign to convince Madayanti, and the king gives him one.
shots.B14C058S01H02: Saudasa says he has no refuge and asks Utanka to take the ear-rings; Madayanti gives them, and Utanka asks Saudasa what his words meant.
shots.B14C058S01H03: Saudasa explains that a king hostile to Brahmanas cannot prosper, and that he gave the ear-rings because he sees no refuge; he asks Utanka to keep the promise.
shots.B14C058S01H04: Utanka promises to return, but asks a question first.
shots.B14C058S01H05: Saudasa says he will answer whatever Utanka asks.
shots.B14C058S02H01: Utanka asks whether he should return to the cannibal king, since the two are now friends.
shots.B14C058S02H02: Saudasa advises him not to return, since he will die if he comes back.
shots.B14C058S02H03: Utanka takes the ear-rings and sets out; he hangs them in his deer-skin in a tree, and fruit falls and loosens the knot, so a Naga of Airavata's race steals them into an anthill, and Utanka digs with his staff for thirty-five days.
shots.B14C058S02H04: Indra, disguised as a Brahmana, tells Utanka that his purpose cannot be achieved with a staff, since the Naga world is far away.
shots.B14C058S02H05: Utanka says he will give up his life before Indra's eyes if he does not recover the ear-rings.
shots.B14C058S03H01: Indra fuses his thunderbolt with Utanka's staff, the earth opens, and Utanka enters the Naga world, which he finds rich and splendid.
shots.B14C058S03H02: Utanka asks how he knew the steed who appears to him at the gate of the Naga world.
shots.B14C058S03H03: The steed, who is the fire-god and his old teacher's teacher, asks Utanka to blow into its body; smoke fills the Naga world, the Nagas bow to Utanka and return the ear-rings, and Utanka brings them to Ahalya and tells Gautama what happened.

B14C059.summary: After granting the boon to Utanka, Krishna goes with Satyaki to Dvaraka, arriving during the festival of Raivataka hill, which is lit and filled with song and generous gifts. The Vrishnis and their allies greet him, and he honours his kin and then his parents. He sits among the Vrishnis and recounts the great battle to his father, which closes the account of this episode.

scenes.B14C059S01: Janamejaya asks what Krishna did next; Vaisampayana describes Krishna's return to Dvaraka during the festival, his welcome by the Vrishnis and his parents, and his account of the battle.
