shots.B14C059S01H01: Janamejaya asks what Govinda did after granting the boon to Utanka.
shots.B14C059S01H02: Vaisampayana describes Krishna's journey to Dvaraka with Satyaki, the festival on Raivataka hill with its lights, songs and gifts, the welcome of his kin, his embrace by his parents, and his account of the great battle to his father.

B14C060.summary: Vasudeva asks Krishna to describe the great battle, since Krishna witnessed it, and Krishna recounts how the commanders fell one by one: Bhishma, Drona, Karna, Salya, Sakuni and finally Duryodhana. He ends with the night slaughter of the Pandava camp by Drona's son, which left only the five Pandavas and a few allies alive. The Vrishnis are shaken by the account, which closes the war's narrative in the Aswamedhika Parva.

scenes.B14C060S01: Vasudeva asks Krishna to describe the battle; Krishna lists the commanders and their falls from Bhishma to Duryodhana, and the night slaughter, and the Vrishnis grieve.

shots.B14C060S01H01: Vasudeva asks Krishna to describe the great battle, which Krishna witnessed, including the Kuru and Pandava leaders.
shots.B14C060S01H02: Vaisampayana says that Krishna described the slaughter of the Kaurava heroes before his father and mother.
shots.B14C060S01H03: Krishna describes the commanders in turn: Bhishma falls to Sikhandin, Drona is slain by Dhrishtadyumna, Karna falls to Arjuna, Salya to Yudhishthira, Sakuni to Sahadeva, Duryodhana to Bhima in a lake, and the Pandava camp is slain at night by Drona's son, leaving only the five Pandavas and a few allies alive.
shots.B14C060S01H04: Vaisampayana says that the Vrishnis, hearing the account, are filled with grief and sorrow.

B14C063.summary: Janamejaya asks how Yudhishthira obtained the wealth that Marutta buried in the earth. Yudhishthira calls his brothers together and asks how they can bring the wealth home, and Bhima proposes that they worship Shiva, whose Kinnara guardians would give up the treasure if the god is pleased. The brothers agree, and the Pandavas set out on the day of the favourable constellation after making offerings to Maheshvara.

scenes.B14C063S01: Janamejaya asks how the buried wealth was obtained; Yudhishthira consults his brothers, Bhima proposes worshipping Shiva, and the Pandavas set out after offerings.

shots.B14C063S01H01: Janamejaya asks what steps Yudhishthira took to obtain the wealth Marutta buried.
shots.B14C063S01H02: Yudhishthira consults his brothers on how to bring the buried wealth; Bhima proposes worshipping Shiva to win over the Kinnaras guarding the treasure, and the brothers agree, make offerings, and set out under a favourable constellation, after taking leave of the elders.

B14C064.summary: The Pandavas set out with a cheerful army, their praises sung by bards, and cross lakes, rivers, forests and mountains until they reach the place where the wealth is buried. Yudhishthira makes camp in a level, auspicious place, placing learned Brahmanas and his priest Agnivesya in the front. The Brahmanas advise a day of fasting and drinking only water, so the brothers spend the night on kusa grass and listen to learned talk until morning.

scenes.B14C064S01: The army marches cheerfully to the buried treasure; Yudhishthira makes camp under the guidance of Brahmanas, and the brothers fast and listen to learned talk through the night.

shots.B14C064S01H01: The army marches cheerfully, crossing lakes, rivers, forests and mountains, and Yudhishthira reaches the spot where the wealth is buried, makes camp with Brahmanas in front, and the Brahmanas call for a fast of water alone while the brothers pass the night on kusa grass.

B14C065.summary: The Brahmanas advise offerings to Mahadeva before the excavation, and the priest Dhaumya performs rites with cakes, flowers and food for Shiva, his attendants, Kubera and the Yakshas. The king gives away cattle, prays to the lord of treasures and his gems, and has the ground dug, and the buried vessels and coins are carried away on camels, horses, elephants and carts. The Pandavas then return toward Hastinapura with the wealth, marching a short distance each day and gladdening the Kurus.

scenes.B14C065S01: Offerings are made to Shiva, his attendants and the Yakshas; the treasure is excavated and loaded onto animals and vehicles; the Pandavas return to the city with it.

shots.B14C065S01H01: The Brahmanas advise offerings to Mahadeva; Dhaumya performs rites with cakes and flowers for Shiva, his attendants, Kubera and the Yakshas; Yudhishthira gives cattle to the Brahmanas, digs up the buried vessels and coins, loads them onto camels, elephants and other vehicles, and returns to the city, marching short stages and cheering the Kurus.

B14C061.summary: Krishna has left out the death of Abhimanyu from his account, so that Vasudeva would not be grieved, but Subhadra asks to hear of her son and faints. Vasudeva, too, falls senseless with grief, and when he recovers he asks how Abhimanyu died. Krishna describes how the boy fought bravely, was surrounded by the Kaurava heroes, and fell to the son of Dussasana. Subhadra mourns with Draupadi and Uttara, and Kunti comforts them and arranges the funeral rites for Abhimanyu.

scenes.B14C061S01: Krishna's account of the battle omits Abhimanyu's death; Subhadra asks for it and faints, Vasudeva falls too, Krishna describes Abhimanyu's death, and Kunti comforts the mourners and arranges rites.

shots.B14C061S01H01: Vaisampayana says that Krishna left out Abhimanyu's death to spare their father, that Subhadra asks to hear of it and faints, that Vasudeva falls senseless too, and that when he recovers he asks Krishna how his grandson died, whether he fought bravely, and whether he was killed by deceit, then Krishna describes the fall of Abhimanyu, Subhadra's grief with Draupadi and Uttara, and Kunti's comfort and arrangements for the rites.

B14C062.summary: Vasudeva performs the funeral rites for Abhimanyu and feeds many thousands of Brahmanas, but his kin, the Pandavas and Uttara remain grieving. Vyasa appears, promises that Uttara will bear a son who will rule after the Pandavas, and tells Arjuna that his grandson will be a great king. He then urges Yudhishthira to hold the horse sacrifice, and the king turns his mind to gathering the wealth needed for it.

scenes.B14C062S01: Vasudeva holds Abhimanyu's rites and gives generously; Vyasa comforts the mourners and promises a grandson for Arjuna, then urges Yudhishthira to fetch wealth for the horse sacrifice.

shots.B14C062S01H01: Vaisampayana says that Vasudeva performs Abhimanyu's rites and feeds many Brahmanas, while the Pandavas and Uttara remain grieving; Vyasa then appears, promises Uttara a son who will rule after the Pandavas and tells Arjuna his grandson will be a high-souled prince, and urges Yudhishthira to hold the horse sacrifice, so the king sets his mind on the journey to bring wealth.

B14C066.summary: Vasudeva returns to the Kuru capital with the Vrishnis, as Yudhishthira asked, for the horse sacrifice. There he finds that Uttara's child, Abhimanyu's son, has been born dead after Ashvatthama's Brahma-weapon struck the womb. Kunti begs Krishna to revive the boy, recalling his earlier promise and Abhimanyu's wish that his son be raised among the Vrishnis, and she falls to the ground in grief until Krishna lifts her up.

scenes.B14C066S01: Vasudeva returns to Hastinapura, where the child is found stillborn after Ashvatthama's weapon; Kunti begs Krishna to revive him, and collapses until Krishna comforts her.

shots.B14C066S01H01: Vaisampayana describes Vasudeva returning to the Kuru capital for the horse sacrifice with his kin, and the birth of Parikshit, who lies lifeless after Ashvatthama's weapon; Kunti meets Krishna in tears, begs him to revive the child as he once promised, and falls to the ground; Krishna lifts her and comforts her.

B14C067.summary: Subhadra, Krishna's sister, joins the lament and says that the child's death will make the Pandavas feel cheated, and that she will die if Krishna does not keep his earlier vow. She recalls how Krishna once promised to revive the child of Kiritin's son when Ashvatthama sought to destroy the unborn child, and asks him to fulfil that vow.

scenes.B14C067S01: Subhadra grieves over the dead child, pleads with Krishna to fulfil his earlier promise to revive him, and says that she will die if he does not.

shots.B14C067S01H01: Subhadra grieves over the dead child, blames Ashvatthama's weapon, recalls Krishna's earlier promise to save the child of Kiritin's son, and begs him to revive the child, or she will die.

B14C068.summary: Krishna agrees to revive the child, and enters the lying-in room, which has been prepared with protective rites and fires. Draupadi brings Uttara to him, and Uttara laments that her child is dead, wishes that she had died instead, and asks Krishna to revive him. The chapter sets the scene for Krishna's act of restoring the child.

scenes.B14C068S01: Krishna agrees to act, enters the prepared lying-in room, and Uttara, with Draupadi, begs him to revive her child, blaming Ashvatthama's cruelty and her own wish to die.

shots.B14C068S01H01: Krishna agrees to revive the child, enters the prepared birth chamber, and Uttara, brought there by Draupadi, laments her dead child and begs Krishna to revive him, with her own life at stake.

B14C069.summary: Uttara faints in grief, and the palace becomes a house of mourning. When she revives, she addresses her child and then bows to Krishna, begging him to save the boy. Krishna withdraws the Brahma-weapon and vows, by his own truth and by his friendship with Arjuna, that the child will live, and the child begins to stir.

scenes.B14C069S01: Uttara faints, revives, begs Krishna to save her son, and Krishna withdraws the weapon with a vow on his truthfulness; the child begins to move.

shots.B14C069S01H01: Uttara faints, the palace is filled with mourning, Uttara revives and begs Krishna to save her child, and Krishna vows on his own truth to revive the child, which then begins to move.

B14C070.summary: When Krishna withdraws the Brahma-weapon, the birth chamber is lit by the child's father's energy, the Rakshasas flee, and a heavenly voice praises Krishna. The child revives, and Krishna gives gifts and names him Parikshit, because he was born when the race was nearly extinct. When the infant is a month old, the Pandavas return to the capital with great wealth, and the city is decked out in celebration.

scenes.B14C070S01: Krishna withdraws the weapon, the child revives and is named Parikshit, and the Pandavas return with wealth to a city decked for celebration.

shots.B14C070S01H01: After the weapon is withdrawn, the child revives, heavenly praise is heard, Krishna gives gifts and names the child Parikshit, and a month later the Pandavas return with their treasure to a city hung with garlands and banners.

B14C071.summary: Vasudeva goes out to meet the Pandavas, who return to Hastinapura with the treasure in their van and pay their respects to Dhritarashtra, Gandhari, Kunti, Vidura and Yuyutsu. Vyasa visits, and Yudhishthira asks his leave to spend the treasure on the horse sacrifice, which Vyasa grants. Yudhishthira then asks Krishna to take up the rites of initiation and lead the sacrifice, and Krishna accepts, pledging to do whatever is asked, with the brothers to take part.

scenes.B14C071S01: Vasudeva greets the Pandavas, who enter the city with the treasure and honour the elders; Vyasa grants leave for the horse sacrifice; Yudhishthira asks Krishna to take part, and Krishna agrees to help.

shots.B14C071S01H01: Vasudeva goes out with his ministers to see the Pandavas.
shots.B14C071S01H02: The Pandavas enter Hastinapura with the treasure in their van, worship Dhritarashtra, Gandhari, Kunti, Vidura and Yuyutsu, and hear of Parikshit's birth; after some days Vyasa comes, and Yudhishthira asks his leave to spend the treasure on the horse sacrifice.
shots.B14C071S01H03: Vyasa grants leave and urges Yudhishthira to perform the horse sacrifice, which cleanses all sins.
shots.B14C071S01H04: Yudhishthira asks Krishna to take up the rites of initiation and lead the sacrifice, calling him the goal of all creatures and the highest preceptor.
shots.B14C071S01H05: Krishna accepts, calls Yudhishthira the king and the senior, and pledges to do all he is asked, with the brothers taking part in the sacrifice.

B14C072.summary: Yudhishthira asks Vyasa to perform his initiation, and Vyasa fixes the full moon of Chaitra for the rite and tells him to choose a horse and let it roam freely. The necessary articles are prepared, some of them of gold. Krishna names Arjuna as the one to guard the horse, while Bhima and Nakula guard the city and Sahadeva looks after the invited guests, and Yudhishthira tells Arjuna to avoid battle where he can and invite the kings to the sacrifice.

scenes.B14C072S01: Vyasa agrees to perform the initiation and prepares the horse; Krishna names Arjuna to guard it, with Bhima, Nakula and Sahadeva given other duties.
scenes.B14C072S02: Yudhishthira charges Arjuna to guard the horse and seek friendship rather than battle; Bhima and Nakula guard the city, and Sahadeva looks after the guests.

shots.B14C072S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Vyasa to perform his initiation at the proper time, as the sacrifice depends on him.
shots.B14C072S01H02: Vyasa fixes the rite for the full moon of Chaitra and tells Yudhishthira to choose a horse, have it roam the earth, and have the necessaries prepared.
shots.B14C072S01H03: Yudhishthira agrees, gathers the articles, and tells Vyasa all is ready; Vyasa asks that the articles be made of gold and that the horse be released.
shots.B14C072S01H04: Yudhishthira asks Vyasa who will guard the horse as it roams the earth.
shots.B14C072S01H05: Krishna names Arjuna to guard the horse, and names Bhima, Nakula and Sahadeva to their tasks; Yudhishthira carries out the instructions and appoints Arjuna.
shots.B14C072S02H01: Yudhishthira tells Arjuna to protect the horse, avoid battle where possible, and invite the kings to the sacrifice.
shots.B14C072S02H02: Vaisampayana says that Yudhishthira orders Bhima and Nakula to guard the city and sets Sahadeva to attend the guests.

B14C073.summary: The initiation is performed, and Yudhishthira shines in his sacrificial garb. The horse is released by Vyasa, and Arjuna follows it on his white-horsed chariot with Gandiva, while the crowds and Brahmanas bless him. The horse roams from the north toward the east, and Arjuna fights many kings, from the Kiratas and Yavanas to other tribes, who have lost kinsmen in the war.

scenes.B14C073S01: The initiation is completed; the horse is released; Arjuna follows it with Gandiva, and the horse roams through many lands where Arjuna fights many kings.

shots.B14C073S01H01: The initiation is completed, Yudhishthira shines in his sacrificial garb, the horse is released by Vyasa, and Arjuna follows it on his chariot while the crowds bless him; the horse roams north and east, and Arjuna fights many kings in many lands.

B14C074.summary: Sons and grandsons of the Trigartas, enemies of the Pandavas, surround Arjuna and try to seize the horse. Arjuna first asks them to desist, recalling Yudhishthira's order not to kill kings whose kin fell at Kurukshetra, but they attack. Arjuna defeats their leader Suryavarman and his brothers, and Dhritavarman wounds him so that Gandiva falls, but he recovers and drives them off. The Trigartas then submit, and Arjuna accepts their surrender.

scenes.B14C074S01: The Trigartas attack Arjuna, who asks them to desist; they refuse, Arjuna defeats their leaders, Gandiva falls after a wound, and the Trigartas submit.

shots.B14C074S01H01: The Trigartas surround Arjuna to seize the horse, Arjuna asks them to desist as Yudhishthira ordered, they refuse, Arjuna defeats Suryavarman and his brothers, Dhritavarman wounds him so that Gandiva falls, Arjuna recovers and routs the Trigartas, and they submit to him.

B14C075.summary: The horse enters the realm of Pragjyotisha, where Vajradatta, son of Bhagadatta, seizes it and carries it back toward his city. Arjuna's arrows make him release the horse and flee, but he returns on his war elephant and challenges Arjuna. Arjuna cuts down his arrows, wounds him, and the elephant is pierced and bleeds heavily as the battle goes on.

scenes.B14C075S01: Vajradatta seizes the horse and is driven off by Arjuna; he returns on an elephant, and Arjuna cuts through his arrows and wounds him and his beast.

shots.B14C075S01H01: The horse enters Pragjyotisha, Vajradatta seizes it, Arjuna's arrows force him to flee, and he returns on an elephant; Arjuna cuts down his arrows, wounds Vajradatta, and pierces the elephant, which bleeds heavily.

B14C076.summary: The battle with Vajradatta lasts three days, and on the fourth day Vajradatta taunts Arjuna about killing his old father Bhagadatta, and charges him on the elephant. Arjuna brings the elephant down with an arrow and, recalling Yudhishthira's order not to slay kings who yield, spares Vajradatta. Vajradatta submits and agrees to attend the sacrifice on the full moon of Chaitra.

scenes.B14C076S01: On the fourth day Vajradatta taunts Arjuna and charges, Arjuna fells the elephant, spares the defeated king on Yudhishthira's instruction, and sends him to the sacrifice.

shots.B14C076S01H01: On the fourth day Vajradatta taunts Arjuna over Bhagadatta's death and charges on his elephant, Arjuna brings the beast down, spares the king on Yudhishthira's order, and the defeated king agrees to attend the sacrifice on the full moon of Chaitra.

B14C077.summary: Arjuna is attacked by hundreds of Saindhavas, who surround him in a cage of cars and shower him with arrows, recalling his slaying of Jayadratha. Omens of disaster appear in heaven and earth, and Arjuna falls stupefied, dropping Gandiva. The gods and sages pray for him, and when his power returns he draws the bow again, scatters the Saindhavas, and drives them off in fear and grief.

scenes.B14C077S01: The Saindhavas surround and wound Arjuna, omens appear, Arjuna falls senseless, the gods pray, and Arjuna recovers and routs his enemies with Gandiva.

shots.B14C077S01H01: The Saindhava warriors surround Arjuna with cars and arrows, omens appear in the sky, Arjuna falls senseless and drops Gandiva, the gods and sages pray for him, and when he recovers he draws Gandiva and scatters the Saindhavas, who flee in grief and fear.

B14C078.summary: Arjuna faces the Saindhavas, but recalls Yudhishthira's order not to kill warriors who come against him, so he tells them to yield and spares whoever admits defeat. As the battle wears on, Dussala, Dhritarashtra's daughter and queen of the Saindhavas, brings her grandson, Suratha's son, to Arjuna, and explains that Suratha died of grief on hearing that Arjuna had slain Jayadratha. Arjuna censures Duryodhana, makes peace, and sends Dussala home, and then follows the horse on to the realm of Manipura.

scenes.B14C078S01: Arjuna fights the Saindhavas but spares those who yield; Dussala brings her grandson, Arjuna makes peace, and the horse moves on to Manipura.

shots.B14C078S01H01: Arjuna, recalling Yudhishthira's order, fights the Saindhavas, cuts down their arrows and weapons, spares those who yield, receives Dussala and her grandson, makes peace, and follows the horse toward Manipura.

B14C079.summary: Vabhruvahana, the ruler of Manipura and Arjuna's son, comes out humbly with gifts to welcome his father, but Arjuna rebukes him for not meeting him as a warrior. The prince is goaded by his mother Ulupi, a Naga princess, into fighting. He wounds Arjuna, who falls senseless, then wakes and praises his son, and their battle continues until the prince pierces his father and the two fall together. Chitrangada, the prince's mother and Arjuna's wife, goes to the field and finds her husband dead.

scenes.B14C079S01: Vabhruvahana comes out with gifts, Arjuna rebukes him, Ulupi urges him to fight, and father and son battle until both fall; Chitrangada arrives and finds her husband slain.

shots.B14C079S01H01: Vabhruvahana comes out with gifts to greet his father Arjuna, who rebukes him for not fighting as a Kshatriya; Ulupi urges her son to fight; the two battle, Arjuna is wounded and falls, the prince is also struck down, and Chitrangada comes to the field and sees her husband dead.

B14C080.summary: Chitrangada blames Ulupi for the death and begs her to revive Arjuna, and then the grieving prince Vabhruvahana, who has killed his father, vows to starve himself or seek expiation. Ulupi then brings a gem that revives the dead and tells the prince that the fight was an illusion she made, for Arjuna's benefit, and that Arjuna cannot truly be defeated. The prince places the gem on his father's chest, and Arjuna revives to the praise of the gods, then asks why the women have come to the field.

scenes.B14C080S01: Chitrangada reproaches Ulupi and asks for Arjuna's life; Vabhruvahana grieves and vows to die; Ulupi brings a gem, reveals the illusion, and Arjuna is revived.

shots.B14C080S01H01: Chitrangada, recovering, blames Ulupi for her husband's death, begs her to revive him, and threatens to starve herself on the battlefield.
shots.B14C080S01H02: Vabhruvahana, grieving, reproaches himself for killing his father, asks the Brahmanas for expiation, and vows to starve himself to death.
shots.B14C080S01H03: Ulupi brings a gem that revives the dead, reveals that the fight was an illusion to test her son and for his father's benefit; the prince places the gem on Arjuna's chest, and Arjuna revives to heavenly praise, and asks why the women are on the field.

B14C081.summary: Arjuna asks Ulupi why she and Chitrangada have come to the battlefield. Ulupi explains that Arjuna had won Bhishma's fall unfairly while Bhishma was fighting Sikhandin, so the Vasus cursed him, and she arranged for his son to defeat him, which freed him from the curse. Arjuna thanks her and tells Vabhruvahana to attend the sacrifice; the prince asks his father to rest in the city first, but Arjuna declines, since his vow keeps him with the wandering horse.

scenes.B14C081S01: Ulupi explains that she arranged Arjuna's defeat by his son to lift the Vasus' curse; Arjuna thanks her, invites his son to the sacrifice, and declines to enter the city while his vow lasts.

shots.B14C081S01H01: Arjuna asks why Ulupi and Chitrangada have come; Ulupi explains that she arranged his defeat by his son to lift the Vasus' curse over his unfair victory against Bhishma; Arjuna thanks her, asks his son to come to the sacrifice, and, since his vow forbids him to enter a city while the horse wanders, leaves with the blessing of his son and wives.

B14C082.summary: The horse turns toward Hastinapura and then to Rajagriha, where Meghasandhi, king of Magadha, challenges Arjuna. Arjuna disarms him, cuts down his chariot and weapons, and spares him, since Yudhishthira ordered that kings who oppose him should not be slain. Meghasandhi submits and promises to attend the sacrifice. The horse then travels along the sea coast into Banga, Pundra and Kosala, where Arjuna defeats many Mlechchha armies.

scenes.B14C082S01: The horse travels to Rajagriha, where Arjuna defeats Meghasandhi, spares him and sends him to the sacrifice, and then the horse goes on to the eastern lands, where Arjuna defeats more armies.

shots.B14C082S01H01: The horse turns toward Hastinapura and then reaches Rajagriha, where Meghasandhi, king of Magadha, challenges Arjuna, is disarmed and spared, and submits; the horse then moves along the coast into Banga, Pundra and Kosala, where Arjuna defeats many Mlechchha armies.

B14C083.summary: The horse passes through the southern lands, including the Chedi city, where Sarabha, son of Shishupala, welcomes Arjuna, and then through the Kasi, Anga, Kosala and Kirata realms, and the country of the Dasarnas, whose king Chitrangada Arjuna subdues. Arjuna defeats the Nishada king, son of Ekalavya, and then the Dravidas, Andhras and other southern peoples, before passing through Surashtra and Prabhasa to Dwaravati. There Ugrasena and Vasudeva greet him with honour, and the horse continues along the western coast toward Gandhara, where a fierce battle with the son of Sakuni begins.

scenes.B14C083S01: The horse travels through many realms, Arjuna subdues or is welcomed by their rulers, and at Dwaravati he is honoured by Ugrasena and Vasudeva before the horse moves on to Gandhara, where Sakuni's son awaits.

shots.B14C083S01H01: The horse travels through the southern and western realms, Arjuna subdues kings and tribes along the way, he is honoured at Dwaravati by Ugrasena and Vasudeva, and the horse then moves toward Gandhara, where a fierce battle with the son of Sakuni is about to begin.

B14C084.summary: The son of Sakuni leads a large Gandhara army against Arjuna, angry at his father's death and at the old feud with the Pandavas. Arjuna first asks the Gandharas to desist, but they surround the horse, and he cuts down many of them. He spares their king, who is unnerved by the defeat, and the king's mother comes out with a welcome and begs her son to stop fighting. Arjuna urges the Gandhara prince to stop the hostility and attend the sacrifice in Chaitra.

scenes.B14C084S01: Sakuni's son leads the Gandharas against Arjuna, who defeats them and spares their king at his mother's request, and urges peace and attendance at the sacrifice.

shots.B14C084S01H01: Sakuni's son leads a large Gandhara army against Arjuna, who defeats his warriors, spares their king at the request of his mother, and urges the king to end hostilities and attend Yudhishthira's sacrifice.

B14C085.summary: Yudhishthira learns that the horse is returning and that Arjuna is well, and sets the time for the sacrifice in the month of Magha. Bhima builds a vast sacrificial ground with golden halls, arches, lodgings for kings and Brahmanas, and sends messengers to invite kings, who bring gifts and attend. Yudhishthira feeds the guests and assigns them food, beds and stables for their animals, and when all is ready, the sacrifice begins. The second part of the chapter describes the crowds of disputants, the splendour of the grounds, and the great feeding of Brahmanas.

scenes.B14C085S01: Yudhishthira hears that Arjuna is returning and sets the sacrifice's date; Bhima builds the grounds, invitations go out, guests arrive, and the sacrifice is ready; the sacrifice begins amid debates, and the kings marvel at the golden grounds, animals and feasts.

shots.B14C085S01H01: Yudhishthira learns that Arjuna is returning with the horse and that Arjuna is well; he sets the date of the sacrifice in the month of Magha, and Bhima builds the sacrificial grounds with golden halls and arches, invites great kings with their gifts, houses the guests and Brahmanas, and arranges food and stables; when all is ready, Yudhishthira rejoices with his brothers.
shots.B14C085S01H02: The sacrifice begins; eloquent debaters argue; the kings marvel at the golden grounds, the great abundance of animals and food, and feasting for Brahmanas and Vaisyas goes on from day to day.

B14C086.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhima to honour the arriving kings, and Krishna comes with the Vrishnis and their leaders. Krishna then reports that a messenger from Arjuna has come, saying that Arjuna is near and worn by many battles. Arjuna's message asks that the kings be honoured, that no massacre like the one at the Rajasuya be allowed, and that Vabhruvahana, his son, be welcomed. Yudhishthira agrees to all of it.

scenes.B14C086S01: Yudhishthira asks Bhima to honour the kings; Krishna arrives and reports Arjuna's message about honouring the kings, avoiding bloodshed, and welcoming Vabhruvahana, and Yudhishthira agrees.

shots.B14C086S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhima to honour the arriving kings; Krishna arrives with the Vrishnis and reports Arjuna's message, sent by an agent, that Arjuna is near and worn by battles, asking that the kings be honoured, that no slaughter like the one at the Rajasuya be allowed, and that Vabhruvahana be welcomed; Yudhishthira approves.

B14C087.summary: Yudhishthira asks why Arjuna always suffers hardship, and Krishna says the only fault he sees is a small feature of his face that keeps him always on the road. Draupadi is angered by the remark, since she cannot bear any fault being found in Arjuna. Arjuna's envoy then arrives with news of his return, and the king, Krishna and Dhritarashtra go out to meet him. Arjuna is welcomed by the citizens, the kings and his brothers, and Vabhruvahana comes to the city with his mothers and goes to Kunti.

scenes.B14C087S01: Yudhishthira asks why Arjuna suffers; Krishna names a minor flaw; Draupadi objects; Arjuna's envoy announces his return, and Arjuna is welcomed; Vabhruvahana arrives with his mothers and goes to Kunti.

shots.B14C087S01H01: Yudhishthira asks why Arjuna always suffers, Krishna names only a small feature of his face as the cause, Draupadi is angered, Arjuna's envoy brings news of his return, Yudhishthira, Krishna and Dhritarashtra go out to meet Arjuna and the citizens praise him, and Vabhruvahana arrives with his mothers and goes to Kunti.

B14C088.summary: Vabhruvahana greets his kin and is given gifts and a golden car by Krishna. Vyasa urges Yudhishthira to begin the sacrifice and to pay three times the usual Dakshina, and Yudhishthira takes the vow and performs the Horse-sacrifice, with the priests carrying out each rite carefully. The stakes and the golden fire altar are set up, and about three hundred animals, including the horse, are bound to them, while celestial beings, sages and musicians attend the sacrifice.

scenes.B14C088S01: Vabhruvahana is welcomed and honoured; Vyasa tells Yudhishthira to begin the sacrifice and pay threefold; the rites are performed, the altar and stakes are set up, and animals are bound, with heavenly beings attending.

shots.B14C088S01H01: Vabhruvahana greets his kin and is honoured with gifts and a golden car; Vyasa tells Yudhishthira to begin the sacrifice and pay threefold Dakshina, which will cleanse him of the sin of slaying his kin; Yudhishthira takes the vow and performs the Horse-sacrifice with carefully ordered rites, golden stakes and a golden altar, and about three hundred animals bound to the stakes, while sages, Gandharvas and Apsaras attend.

B14C089.summary: The priests sacrifice the horse, Draupadi sits beside its body, and its marrow is cooked and offered, completing the rite. Yudhishthira gives away a vast amount of gold and the whole earth to Vyasa, who returns it for a price, and Yudhishthira declares that the Brahmanas should divide the earth. Krishna then gives the earth back to Yudhishthira, who pays millions of coins and triples the Dakshina. The priests divide the wealth, Yudhishthira sends Vabhruvahana home with gifts, and the Vrishnis depart. The great sacrifice is celebrated as a festival, and Yudhishthira returns to his capital cleansed of sin.

scenes.B14C089S01: The horse is sacrificed; Yudhishthira gives the earth to Vyasa, who returns it, and Krishna returns it to Yudhishthira, who pays for it with millions of coins; the wealth is divided, the guests depart, and Yudhishthira returns to his capital.

shots.B14C089S01H01: The priests sacrifice the horse with Draupadi beside its body, its marrow is cooked and offered, Yudhishthira gives a thousand crores of gold and the whole earth to Vyasa, who returns the earth for a price, Krishna then gives it back to Yudhishthira, who pays millions of coins in place of the Dakshina; the priests divide the wealth, the kings and Vabhruvahana are sent home with gifts, Krishna and the Vrishnis leave for Dwaravati, and Yudhishthira, cleansed of sin, returns to his capital.

B14C090.summary: Janamejaya asks for any wonderful incident from his ancestors' sacrifice. At the height of the feasting, a mongoose with half its body turned to gold declares that the great sacrifice is worth less than a small measure of barley given by a poor Brahmana of Kurukshetra. He tells how that Brahmana, his wife, son and daughter-in-law, in a famine, each gave up their share of their last barley to a hungry guest, who turned out to be the god of righteousness and took the family to heaven. The mongoose says that the dust of that barley is what turned half its body to gold, and the Brahmanas return home; Vaisampayana closes by saying that gifts, penance and harmlessness are as meritorious as sacrifice.

scenes.B14C090S01: Janamejaya asks about a wonder at the sacrifice; a golden-half mongoose says the sacrifice is worth less than a small gift of barley, and the Brahmanas ask him to explain.
scenes.B14C090S02: The mongoose recounts how the poor Brahmana and his family each gave their share of barley to a guest, who was the god of righteousness; the mongoose's body was made gold by the barley dust, and Vaisampayana closes by praising gifts and penance over sacrifice.

shots.B14C090S01H01: Janamejaya asks Vaisampayana to tell of a wonderful incident at his ancestors' sacrifice.
shots.B14C090S01H02: At the end of the Horse-sacrifice, while gifts are praised and flowers fall on Yudhishthira, a blue-eyed mongoose, half of it golden, speaks in a voice like thunder, saying the sacrifice is not worth a prastha of barley given by a liberal Brahmana of Kurukshetra.
shots.B14C090S01H03: The mongoose says it will tell the Brahmanas of the Unccha Brahmana, who lived by gleaning with his wife, son and daughter-in-law, and who, in a famine, shared a single prastha of barley with a hungry guest.
shots.B14C090S01H04: The Brahmana, unable to feed the guest, accepts his wife's share and then his son's, and the father says he is old and feels little hunger, so he gives the barley away.
shots.B14C090S01H05: The son says he is his father's offspring, who rescues the father, and asks the father to save himself through him.
shots.B14C090S02H01: The father takes his son's share, gives it to the guest, and the daughter-in-law then offers her share for the sake of the grandchildren and the family's merit.
shots.B14C090S02H02: The father-in-law refuses to take the daughter-in-law's share, since she is weakened by hunger, and says it would be wrong.
shots.B14C090S02H03: The daughter-in-law insists that the father-in-law is the god of her god and that she is devoted to him, and asks him to take her share.
shots.B14C090S02H04: The Brahmana takes her share and gives it to the guest, who reveals himself as the god of righteousness, praises the gift, and invites the family to heaven, where they ascend; the mongoose then says the barley dust and the water left behind made half its body gold, and that the Horse-sacrifice has not made the rest golden, so the gift is greater than the sacrifice.
shots.B14C090S02H05: Vaisampayana closes the story by saying that sacrifice should not be overvalued, since penance, harmlessness, contentment, sincerity, self-restraint, truth and gifts equal it in merit.

B14C091.summary: Janamejaya asks why the mongoose belittled the great Horse-sacrifice, when sacrifices are known to win heaven. Vaisampayana recounts an early sacrifice of Indra, where the sages objected to killing animals and proposed grain offerings instead, but the dispute was settled by King Vasu, who gave a false judgment and was sent to the nether world. Vaisampayana concludes that gifts from unrighteous wealth carry no merit, while modest gifts of lawfully gathered food or water, made with a pure heart, win heaven, as examples of ancient kings show.

scenes.B14C091S01: Janamejaya asks why the mongoose belittled the sacrifice; Vaisampayana tells of the dispute at Indra's sacrifice, King Vasu's false judgment, and the lesson that lawful and sincere giving is what brings merit.

shots.B14C091S01H01: Janamejaya asks why the mongoose belittled the great Horse-sacrifice, since kings and sages win heaven through sacrifices and Yudhishthira is a model of prosperity.
shots.B14C091S01H02: Vaisampayana recounts the sacrifice of Indra, where the sages objected to killing animals and asked for grain; the dispute was referred to King Vasu, who answered falsely and was cast into the nether world, and Vaisampayana concludes that unlawful wealth gives no merit while lawful and sincere gifts, of grain, fruit or water, bring heaven, as the example of ancient kings shows.

B14C092.summary: Janamejaya asks how lawful wealth can win heaven, and Vaisampayana tells of Agastya's twelve-year sacrifice, in which Indra withheld rain until Agastya's penance and the sages' request brought it back. The story then explains that the golden mongoose was Anger, cursed by the Pitris after it spoiled a sage's milk, and that it disparaged Yudhishthira's sacrifice to be freed. The Parva closes here, and the translator's notes follow.

scenes.B14C092S01: Janamejaya asks how the reward of lawful wealth compares with sacrifice; Vaisampayana tells of Agastya's long sacrifice, Indra's withheld rain, and the sages' call for harmless, lawful offerings, then explains who the golden mongoose was.
scenes.B14C092S02: Jamadagni sends Anger away, the Pitris tell it how to end its curse by disparaging Dharma, and the mongoose ends its curse at Yudhishthira's sacrifice; the Parva closes and the translator's notes begin.
scenes.B14C092S03: Translator's Notes 3 to 7, on Marutta's gold, the naked ascetics, and some commentary readings.
scenes.B14C092S04: Translator's Notes 8 to 12, on the yogic absorption, the great dissolution, the seven questions and the rules of health.
scenes.B14C092S05: Translator's Notes 13 to 17, on the body's dissolution at death, rebirth in the womb, and the readings of the commentators.
scenes.B14C092S06: Translator's Notes 18 to 22, on how the soul enters the body, the causes of its changes, and the three elements of the universe.
scenes.B14C092S07: Translator's Notes 23 to 27, on the stages of Yoga, the one receptacle of all things, and the nature of the self.
scenes.B14C092S08: Translator's Notes 28 to 32, on nirvana, the destruction of impressions, and the concentration that frees.
scenes.B14C092S09: Translator's Notes 33 to 37, on seeing the Supreme Soul in trance and resisting the temptations of Indra.
scenes.B14C092S10: Translator's Notes 38 to 42, on the centres of the body in Yoga, the vision of Brahman, and the form of the Soul.
scenes.B14C092S11: Translator's Notes 43 to 47, on who is speaking, the path of action and the path of knowledge, and the wife's question to her husband.
scenes.B14C092S12: Translator's Notes 48 to 52, on the seat of Brahman in the body and the life-breaths.
scenes.B14C092S13: Translator's Notes 53 to 57, on the inner sacrifice with its priests and fires, and the dispute between Word and Mind.
scenes.B14C092S14: Translator's Notes 58 to 62, on words, the mind, and the verses about Word.
scenes.B14C092S15: Translator's Notes 63 to 67, on the senses' argument with the mind and the three qualities as smoke, ash and flame.
scenes.B14C092S16: Translator's Notes 68 to 72, on action, agent and instrument, and on the sacrifice of the senses.
scenes.B14C092S17: Translator's Notes 73 to 77, on the teacher, the inner forest, and its seven trees and fruits.
scenes.B14C092S18: Translator's Notes 78 to 82, on the states of non-being, the senses, and the story of Rama's campaigns.
scenes.B14C092S19: Translator's Notes 83 to 87, on Alarka's Yoga, the joy of attaining, and the inner foes.
scenes.B14C092S20: Translator's Notes 88 to 92, on Janaka's detachment and the reading of his verses.
scenes.B14C092S21: Translator's Notes 93 to 97, on Janaka's choice of knowledge, the stages of life, and action and understanding.
scenes.B14C092S22: Translator's Notes 98 to 102, on how release comes through seeing and hearing, and on souls merging into Brahman.
scenes.B14C092S23: Translator's Notes 103 to 107, on the qualities of the elements, the eleven, and rebirth as animals.
scenes.B14C092S24: Translator's Notes 108 to 112, on the three qualities in creation and the seasons.
scenes.B14C092S25: Translator's Notes 113 to 117, on the mind's reach, rebirth as a Brahmana, and a passage repeated by error.
scenes.B14C092S26: Translator's Notes 118 to 122, on the readings of the verses, the two deities, and the body as the wheel of Time.
scenes.B14C092S27: Translator's Notes 123 to 127, on readings, the names of trees, and the Apsaras.
scenes.B14C092S28: Translator's Notes 128 to 132, on the humility of good men, the role of Nature in knowledge, and the wheel of life.
scenes.B14C092S29: Translator's Notes 133 to 137, on the wheel of life, the student's duties, and sacred foods and woods.
scenes.B14C092S30: Translator's Notes 138 to 142, on the stages of a renunciant's life, how he begs and bathes, and the self.
scenes.B14C092S31: Translator's Notes 143 to 147, on the Vedas, the limbs of Yoga, and the relation of Purusha and Nature.
scenes.B14C092S32: Translator's Notes 148 to 152, on knowledge as the means of life's journey and the image of the car.
scenes.B14C092S33: Translator's Notes 153 to 157, on the stages of action, the musical scale, and the understanding.
scenes.B14C092S34: Translator's Notes 158 to 162, on the true Veda, mineness and death, and the sixteen.
scenes.B14C092S35: Translator's Notes 163 to 167, on the unreality of the world in trance, and on Hastinapura and Vasudeva.
scenes.B14C092S36: Translator's Notes 168 to 172, on forgiveness, the teacher's fee, and Saudasa's curse.
scenes.B14C092S37: Translator's Notes 173 to 177, on the king's refuge, Utanka's truthfulness, and some names.
scenes.B14C092S38: Translator's Notes 178 to 182, on names, the constellation, Dhaumya, and the layout of the camp.
scenes.B14C092S39: Translator's Notes 183 to 187, on the treasure carts, the water rite, and some names.

shots.B14C092S01H01: Janamejaya asks how heaven can come from lawfully earned wealth, and asks Vaisampayana to explain the surety of the highest end in sacrifice.
shots.B14C092S01H02: Vaisampayana begins the tale of Agastya's great sacrifice, which lasted twelve years, during which Indra withheld rain and the rishis worried about the food supply.
shots.B14C092S01H03: The rishis say that Agastya's sacrifice has been made with lawful gifts, but that Indra's withheld rain now threatens it, and they ask him to keep his power in check.
shots.B14C092S01H04: Janamejaya asks who the golden-headed mongoose was and how it spoke a human language.
shots.B14C092S01H05: Vaisampayana says that Anger, taking the form of Dharma, spoiled the milk of the sage Jamadagni, and that Anger was overcome by the sage's forgiveness and then cursed to be a mongoose.
shots.B14C092S02H01: Jamadagni tells Anger to go freely, since no harm was done; the Pitris tell Anger that disparaging Dharma will end its curse, and the mongoose disparaged the sacrifice of Yudhishthira, freeing it, since Yudhishthira is Dharma's self.
shots.B14C092S02H02: Heading: the Aswamedha Parva ends here.
shots.B14C092S02H04: Note 1: the epithet 'Mahavahu' occurs twice in one passage, and one epithet is left out as redundant.
shots.B14C092S02H05: Note 2: 'human sacrifice' is meant, which suggests that human sacrifice was once practised.
shots.B14C092S03H01: Note 3: Marutta's Himalayan sacrifice gave so much gold that the Brahmanas could carry only part of it and threw away the rest.
shots.B14C092S03H03: Note 5: 'Nityada' means always; the word is dropped as repetitive.
shots.B14C092S03H04: Note 6: Nilakantha reads a phrase as 'no own self' and takes the vocative 'vibho' as the Supreme Self.
shots.B14C092S03H05: Note 7: 'agatagamam' means one who has grasped the secret of the scriptures.
shots.B14C092S04H01: Note 8: 'nirakara' means reliance on Brahman through Yoga absorption, a state of perfect unconsciousness.
shots.B14C092S04H02: Note 9: the dissolution meant is the great final one, not the partial ones; until then the sage sees beings pass through repeated births.
shots.B14C092S04H03: Note 10: the commentator counts seven questions: the body's dissolution, re-acquiring a body, escaping rebirth, the causes of embodiment, final absorption, the enjoyment of deeds, and deeds without a body.
shots.B14C092S04H04: Note 11: 'kala' means both season and stage of life, so food suited to one may not suit another; the verses follow Charaka's rules of health.
shots.B14C092S04H05: Note 12: the three faults are wind, bile and phlegm, which give health when in harmony and disease when excited; Telang misreads 'doshan' as disorders.
shots.B14C092S05H01: Note 13: 'jivitam' in the second line is the object of 'sariram' in the first.
shots.B14C092S05H02: Note 14: 'garbha-sankramane' means entering a womb after leaving a body; the translator notes that the pains of death match those of birth.
shots.B14C092S05H03: Note 15: 'sambutatwam' means being joined, and 'niyachachati' means perishes; 'Vayu' is to be understood in the second line.
shots.B14C092S05H05: Note 17: Nilakantha reads this verse so that Jiva is unattached through its subtlety; the translator finds this strained.
shots.B14C092S06H01: Note 18: 'chetasa' means the outward covering the soul takes on; 'pranasthaneshu' means the seats of the senses; 'chetana' means mind, not consciousness.
shots.B14C092S06H02: Note 19: the phrase 'causes them to grow' is taken differently from Nilakantha, which the translator does not follow.
shots.B14C092S06H03: Note 20: one of the 'cha' particles marks the cause, hence 'therefore' in the translation.
shots.B14C092S06H04: Note 21: 'vikrita' means altered, not degraded; the pure soul falls from its Brahman state through acts that have no beginning.
shots.B14C092S06H05: Note 22: the verse divides the universe into the perishable, the imperishable and the higher, and every person is a pair of the first two; Telang's version differs and omits 'trayanam'.
shots.B14C092S07H01: Note 23: the order of words in the first line is given as the correct one; Telang's first line is said to differ.
shots.B14C092S07H02: Note 24: 'Ekayana' is Brahman, the one receptacle of all; 'tushni' means silently, without even thinking of oneself; the stages of Yoga merge the grosser into the subtler.
shots.B14C092S07H03: Note 25: Bengal texts read the first half of verse 8 differently, meaning without ease or joy, bound by slavery and ignorance.
shots.B14C092S07H04: Note 26: stripped of these attributes, the Soul is pure consciousness, free of the coverings of ignorance.
shots.B14C092S07H05: Note 27: formlessness means subtlety; 'without cause' means eternal; enjoying attributes without being bound by them marks release.
shots.B14C092S08H01: Note 28: nirvana, in the orthodox view, is the end of separate existence by absorption into Brahman.
shots.B14C092S08H02: Note 29: impressions from outside objects are destroyed by those of contemplation, which must in turn be destroyed before absorption.
shots.B14C092S08H03: Note 30: 'siddham' means free from the errors caused by ignorance.
shots.B14C092S08H04: Note 31: Nilakantha's glosses: 'attman' is the mind, 'atmani' the body, 'charayan' turning inward, and 'nityam' without beginning or end.
shots.B14C092S08H05: Note 32: fixing the mind on the soul is the concentration that frees, possible only after severe austerities.
shots.B14C092S09H01: Note 33: the translator expands the verse: on waking from trance the sage sees the universe as nothing but the Supreme Soul.
shots.B14C092S09H02: Note 34: an alternative sense: he has no superior, not even the Lord of the universe.
shots.B14C092S09H03: Note 35: the first line is doubtful; the sense is that such a person becomes god of the gods, and 'karayate' may be read as 'karoti'.
shots.B14C092S09H04: Note 36: the translator follows Nilakantha: one should not fall from Yoga, tempted by its powers; Telang's version differs.
shots.B14C092S09H05: Note 37: only a yogin who has not advanced far is tempted by pleasure; an adept can dismiss Indra himself, as Diogenes dismissed Alexander.
shots.B14C092S10H01: Note 38: verses 33 to 37 are rendered close to the text following Nilakantha; the 'city' is the body with its centres, and once Brahman is known the mind has nothing else to rest on.
shots.B14C092S10H02: Note 39: that from which the universe is made, meaning Brahman.
shots.B14C092S10H03: Note 40: probably 'by any of the senses'; the original has the plural.
shots.B14C092S10H04: Note 41: this answers the questions about the form of the Soul, according to Nilakantha.
shots.B14C092S10H05: Note 42: following Nilakantha, the yogin rises from Brahma with attributes to Brahma without them, and 'deheswam dharayan' means holding the mind within the body.
shots.B14C092S11H01: Note 43: the speaker is the visitor whom Krishna repeats; Krishna, forgetting he is quoting, speaks as the Supreme Brahman in whom one merges.
shots.B14C092S11H02: Note 44: the second line of verse 56 has several readings.
shots.B14C092S11H03: Note 45: heaven rewards action, while release through knowledge is higher than the state of the gods, which is why the gods envy those who attain it.
shots.B14C092S11H04: Note 46: 'avichakshanam' means undiscerning: the husband does not see that his wife has no refuge but him, with all his faults.
shots.B14C092S11H05: Note 47: following Nilakantha, 'grahyam' means acts done with others' help, like initiation; Telang follows another commentator.
shots.B14C092S12H01: Note 48: Nilakantha calls this seat Avimukta, lying between the eyebrows and the nose.
shots.B14C092S12H02: Note 49: Nilakantha reads Soma as the Ida duct and Agni as the Pingala duct, which meet where Brahman dwells, with Vayu urging the understanding.
shots.B14C092S12H03: Note 50: 'yatra' here means 'for which', not a place.
shots.B14C092S12H04: Note 51: 'tasmin' means Prana joined with Apana, per Nilakantha.
shots.B14C092S12H05: Note 52: Udana is named for its upward movement; penance controls Udana, ends rebirth and leads to absorption in Brahman.
shots.B14C092S13H01: Note 53: those who give up sense objects can create them at will; one who gives up smell, which belongs to earth, can create earth.
shots.B14C092S13H02: Note 54: the senses are the priests pouring libations, their perceptions are the offerings, the elements are the fires, and the sense objects are the fuel; verse 5 repeats this.
shots.B14C092S13H03: Note 55: the heart is the household fire, the mind the offering fire, and speech comes from food or fire poured into the mouth; the translator compares this with the Genesis account of creation by the word.
shots.B14C092S13H04: Note 56: in dreamless sleep the mind vanishes while Prana continues, so the question is why Prana then does not perceive.
shots.B14C092S13H05: Note 57: 'bhutatmanam' means ordinary Prajapati, which Nilakantha takes as the individual self.
shots.B14C092S14H01: Note 58: desirable fruits, seen and unseen, come through words, meaning both ordinary speech and Vedic mantras.
shots.B14C092S14H02: Note 59: the translator suggests the Brahmana repeats Jiva's answer to Word; the immovable mind is what the senses grasp, the movable mind lies beyond them, and the mind relies on word and scripture.
shots.B14C092S14H03: Note 60: Telang's version of this verse differs; the translator gives only a verbal rendering.
shots.B14C092S14H04: Note 61: the phrase means noisy or noiseless.
shots.B14C092S14H05: Note 62: the translator gives a close rendering but finds the sense obscure, as are Nilakantha's gloss and Telang's version; the vernacular versions are of little use.
shots.B14C092S15H01: Note 63: the proper reading puts 'cha' after 'arthan', so the Senses say that enjoyment is impossible without them and their objects.
shots.B14C092S15H02: Note 64: creatures can live through the senses even when the mind is out of order.
shots.B14C092S15H03: Note 65: both mental purposes and dreams fail to satisfy the one who relies on them.
shots.B14C092S15H04: Note 66: the smoke is darkness, the ashes passion, and the flame into which the oblation is cast is goodness; the reading 'sarvam' is wrong.
shots.B14C092S15H05: Note 67: the translator gives a close rendering that does not follow the commentators, notes that the printed texts differ, and that the order of the verses varies.
shots.B14C092S16H01: Note 68: 'these' means action, agent and instrument, each carrying the qualities of goodness, passion and darkness.
shots.B14C092S16H02: Note 69: it is the senses, not the soul, that enjoy; the ignorant take themselves for their senses and possessions, though they are really the self.
shots.B14C092S16H03: Note 70: the senses, mind and their objects are to be offered as libations on the inner fire of the soul.
shots.B14C092S16H04: Note 71: truth is the Sastra of the Prasastri.
shots.B14C092S16H05: Note 72: Narayana stands for the Veda or the Soul, and the animals once offered to him were the senses.
shots.B14C092S17H01: Note 73: 'srota' means a preceptor or one who dispels doubts; 'amaratwam' is the state of the immortal head of all.
shots.B14C092S17H02: Note 74: the translator disagrees with Telang: the Soul is both teacher and student, and there is no other teacher.
shots.B14C092S17H03: Note 75: the one who understands the truth.
shots.B14C092S17H04: Note 76: the seven trees are the five senses, mind and understanding; the fruits are their pleasures and pains; the guests are the powers of the senses; the hermitages are where the guests rest; the seven Yogas are the stilling of the senses, and the seven initiations are giving up their actions one by one.
shots.B14C092S17H05: Note 77: the correct readings are 'bhavantyanityah' and 'vahuswabhavan'.
shots.B14C092S18H01: Note 78: 'swabhava' means utter non-being, according to Nilakantha.
shots.B14C092S18H02: Note 79: the life-winds stand for the organs of action, the tongue for the senses, the mind for inner acts, goodness for pleasure and passion for pain; freedom from these transcends sin, and knowledge is the means.
shots.B14C092S18H03: Note 80: the speaker followed custom and mantras in ignorance, and now that his eyes are open he should not be blamed for his earlier acts.
shots.B14C092S18H04: Note 81: Kshatriyas need Brahmanas for their rites; those who fled from Rama could find none, so their children fell to the status of Vrishalas or Sudras.
shots.B14C092S18H05: Note 82: 'Kshatriya-bandhu' means inferior Kshatriyas, as 'Brahma-bandhu' means inferior Brahmanas, not kinsmen of Kshatriyas.
shots.B14C092S19H01: Note 83: the vocative addresses Jamadagni's son, and the speech is the Pitris' to Rama, repeated by the Brahmana to his wife; the Yoga is Raja-Yoga, whereas Alarka had followed Hatha-Yoga, which often destroys its practitioner.
shots.B14C092S19H02: Note 84: 'praharsha' is joy at the certainty of gaining what is wanted, 'priti' is satisfaction on gaining it, and 'ananda' is joy while enjoying it.
shots.B14C092S19H03: Note 85: the wise man first conquers the inner foes and then the outer obstacles to his release.
shots.B14C092S19H04: Note 86: 'dosha' means attachment and craving; 'sadhu' means the virtues of calm and the like, not men.
shots.B14C092S19H05: Note 87: 'samhatadehabandhanah' means with the bodily bonds united, not destroyed; the translator thinks Telang is wrong.
shots.B14C092S20H01: Note 88: the conditions are affluence and indigence, per Nilakantha.
shots.B14C092S20H02: Note 89: the text refers to the rule 'do not covet another's property'; Janaka asks how one could tell what belongs to others.
shots.B14C092S20H03: Note 90: smell belongs to earth, and Janaka does not desire it for himself, so earth is subject to him; mastering the senses' objects is mastering the world.
shots.B14C092S20H04: Note 91: Janaka lives and acts for these, not for himself.
shots.B14C092S20H05: Note 92: the translator corrects Nilakantha's reading to 'Brahmana-bhasya', notes that 'nemi' can mean the track of a wheel, and that the nave is the Vedas.
shots.B14C092S21H01: Note 93: between rule over earth or heaven and knowledge of identity with the universe, the speaker freely chooses the latter, which is his wealth.
shots.B14C092S21H02: Note 94: these are the different modes of life.
shots.B14C092S21H03: Note 95: the knowledge to be gained is that all is one; there are many paths to it, and those who attain tranquillity have gained it.
shots.B14C092S21H04: Note 96: actions are perishable and give no lasting result, so lasting knowledge must be reached through understanding.
shots.B14C092S21H05: Note 97: the translator expands the verse: good means are seen as bees see flowers; action cleanses understanding, which through ignorance takes on the marks of knowledge; 'karmabudhi' does not mean action and knowledge.
shots.B14C092S22H01: Note 98: for release no positive or negative rules are given; only seeing, meaning contemplation, and hearing, meaning teaching from the preceptor, are prescribed.
shots.B14C092S22H02: Note 99: one begins with contemplation of perceived objects like earth, then unseen mental objects; the practice of calm and self-control leads to the Highest.
shots.B14C092S22H03: Note 100: when her individual soul merges into the Supreme, she becomes Brahman, having come to know Kshetra as distinct from Kshetrajna.
shots.B14C092S22H04: Note 101: their origin is Brahman; they live apart from it through their deeds, and when the deeds cease they merge back into Brahman.
shots.B14C092S22H05: Note 102: the course of life that seeks knowledge of the soul, including the knowledge needed to identify with Brahman.
shots.B14C092S23H01: Note 103: each element has its quality: smell to earth, sound to ether, taste to water; the deities of the last verse are probably the senses.
shots.B14C092S23H02: Note 104: the eleven are the three qualities, the five elements, the senses taken together, egoism and understanding.
shots.B14C092S23H03: Note 105: 'anyatha pratipannah' means born in other orders; those born as goats rise through the Brahmanas' rites and regain their true place by becoming sacrificial victims.
shots.B14C092S23H04: Note 106: 'qualities abiding in darkness' means those permanently attached to darkness.
shots.B14C092S23H05: Note 107: some texts read 'santapah' for 'sanghatah', meaning grief or sorrow.
shots.B14C092S24H01: Note 108: this may mean exposing other people's faults by tearing away their coverings.
shots.B14C092S24H02: Note 109: 'vibhajanti' means enjoyments here; Telang's objection to the word is unnecessary.
shots.B14C092S24H03: Note 110: 'from even a distance' means on a quick view, without close examination.
shots.B14C092S24H04: Note 111: the three qualities exist even in still things: darkness predominates, passion is in changing traits like sourness and sweetness, and goodness in their oily traits; Telang's reading of the first line is untenable.
shots.B14C092S24H05: Note 112: 'conjunctions' are the joining periods between the seasons.
shots.B14C092S25H01: Note 113: probably that the mind, through the senses, enters into all things and knows them.
shots.B14C092S25H02: Note 114: through these one takes birth as a Brahmana.
shots.B14C092S25H03: Note 115: about five verses repeat here, an interpolation caused by carelessness.
shots.B14C092S25H04: Note 116: these are to be regarded as no different from the mind, having no real existence beyond it.
shots.B14C092S25H05: Note 117: 'that' refers to the thinning of all things by their absorption into the mind.
shots.B14C092S26H01: Note 118: 'gunagunam' means treating qualities as not qualities, since bravery and the like breed pride; 'ekacharyyam' means living in seclusion; 'anantaram' means recognising no distinctions; 'ekapadam sukham' is the source of all happiness.
shots.B14C092S26H02: Note 119: the two deities are Jiva and Iswara.
shots.B14C092S26H03: Note 120: the correct reading in verse 53 is 'samsargabhiratam', not 'samsayabhiratam'.
shots.B14C092S26H04: Note 121: the correct words are 'martya' and 'sarva'; release is hard to reach, so the body is like the wheel of Time, always turning.
shots.B14C092S26H05: Note 122: the body is the wheel of Time, the ocean of delusion, and the creator, destroyer and reawakener of the universe, since creatures act through it.
shots.B14C092S27H01: Note 123: 'satah' cannot mean 'the good', since the verses are in the singular.
shots.B14C092S27H02: Note 124: the correct reading ends the first line with 'atmana', not 'atman'.
shots.B14C092S27H04: Note 126: the trees named are the banyan, rose apple, peepal, silk-cotton, sissoo, Asclepias and a mountain bamboo; here Kichaka probably means the neem.
shots.B14C092S27H05: Note 127: the second line may be read with 'strinam' referring to women and 'vasumatyah' as an adjective of the Apsaras.
shots.B14C092S28H01: Note 128: good men do not let others know their acts; they avoid show.
shots.B14C092S28H02: Note 129: the sense of self and the distinction of things come from Prakriti, Nature.
shots.B14C092S28H03: Note 130: 'Savitri' here covers all forms of worship, by Brahmanas and even by Mlecchas; the translator calls this a looking back, like a lion.
shots.B14C092S28H04: Note 131: Brahman is above the Prajapatis and Vishnu above Brahman; the translator thinks Telang misreads this.
shots.B14C092S28H05: Note 132: the spokes are the 'bandhanam', the nave is 'pariskandha', and home is the rim, since it limits affections and acts as the rim limits a wheel.
shots.B14C092S29H01: Note 133: the wheel phrase recurs; the translator reads 'asaktaprabhavapavyam' differently from Nilakantha and cannot find the source of Telang's 'never fatigued'.
shots.B14C092S29H02: Note 134: the student should go to his teacher's house, study and serve there, and then return to family life.
shots.B14C092S29H03: Note 135: the last three duties bring merit; the first three are the means of livelihood.
shots.B14C092S29H04: Note 136: Havishya is food cooked without meat in a single vessel, with milk or ghee allowed, and offered to the gods.
shots.B14C092S29H05: Note 137: Vilwa is Aegle marmelos, and Palasa is Butea frondosa.
shots.B14C092S30H01: Note 138: the forest dweller eats fruits, roots and leaves first, then drinks water, then breathes air; the sects differ, and the path is set at initiation.
shots.B14C092S30H02: Note 139: the renouncer begs only where cooking is finished and everyone has eaten, so he is not overfed by a householder who sees him.
shots.B14C092S30H03: Note 140: the ascetic should not bathe by plunging into a stream, lake or tank.
shots.B14C092S30H04: Note 141: 'kalakankhi' probably means letting time pass indifferently.
shots.B14C092S30H05: Note 142: the self has no qualities; those who seek it practise these duties, which form the path to it.
shots.B14C092S31H01: Note 143: 'that which has Brahman for its origin' means the Vedas.
shots.B14C092S31H02: Note 144: commentators differ on 'the ten or the twelve'; Nilakantha counts the limbs of Yoga and the four virtues of friendliness, compassion, gladness and equanimity.
shots.B14C092S31H03: Note 145: the Unmanifest is the state where the three qualities are combined; when goodness prevails, Purusha emerges, and their relation is both unity and difference, shown by the gnat and the udumbara, the fish and the water, and the drop and the lotus leaf.
shots.B14C092S31H04: Note 146: the doubts concern whether duties must be done and whether they bear fruit here and hereafter.
shots.B14C092S31H05: Note 147: the thinking or enjoying agent is the subject and what is thought or enjoyed is the object; the translator follows Telang in using these terms.
shots.B14C092S32H01: Note 148: 'sattva pradipa' means the light of Nature, which Nilakantha reads as knowledge; Arjuna Misra's reading is that knowledge of truth comes to the self through Nature.
shots.B14C092S32H02: Note 149: as a traveller needs provisions, so one on life's journey needs knowledge; action is not the proper means, since it may or may not bear fruit.
shots.B14C092S32H03: Note 150: one should not care for external things.
shots.B14C092S32H04: Note 151: once knowledge, the highest seat, is attained, the acts enjoined by scripture need not be done.
shots.B14C092S32H05: Note 152: a car is comfortable only on a car road; where the road fails, the car becomes a burden, so one leaves it.
shots.B14C092S33H01: Note 153: Arjuna Misra's stages are action with desire, action without desire, and then knowledge; Nilakantha lists action, Yoga, and the state of the Hansa or Paramahansa.
shots.B14C092S33H02: Note 154: 'katu' means pungent or sharp, as chili is.
shots.B14C092S33H03: Note 155: these are the notes of the Hindu musical scale.
shots.B14C092S33H04: Note 156: the understanding acts on what the mind presents to it, so it is the lord, served by the mind.
shots.B14C092S33H05: Note 157: 'sarvan srijati' means creating all things by becoming the universal cause, the unmanifest; there is no difference between such a one and the Supreme Soul.
shots.B14C092S34H01: Note 158: one who reads the book called the Veda does not truly know it; one who knows Kshetrajna truly knows the Veda.
shots.B14C092S34H02: Note 159: 'Mrityu' and 'mama' each have two syllables, and 'Brahman' and 'na-mama' have three, which gives the play that mineness is death and its absence is eternal.
shots.B14C092S34H03: Note 160: the sixteen are the five elements, the four organs of knowledge with the mind, and the four organs of action.
shots.B14C092S34H04: Note 161: Purusha here is the embodied self with consciousness of the body, which true knowledge destroys; 'eaters of Amrita' are those who offer food to the gods, ancestors and guests.
shots.B14C092S34H05: Note 162: Purusha here is the individual self freed from consciousness of the body.
shots.B14C092S35H01: Note 163: in a dream all that is seen is unreal; once tranquillity is reached the surroundings are equally unreal, and the Soul dwells in itself.
shots.B14C092S35H02: Note 164: the sages behold all worldly objects, past, present and future, which arise from earlier causes.
shots.B14C092S35H03: Note 165: the Supreme can be known only in the measure He chooses to be known.
shots.B14C092S35H04: Note 166: Vasudeva is Krishna's father and Yudhishthira's maternal uncle; Yudhishthira asks Krishna to convey his respect to Vasudeva and Valadeva.
shots.B14C092S35H05: Note 167: Hastinapura is also called Nagapura, both words meaning elephant; the 'city called after the elephant' is the usual name of the Kuru capital.
shots.B14C092S36H01: Note 168: 'mahyam' means 'for me', referring to Krishna's divine nature.
shots.B14C092S36H02: Note 169: a Brahmana loses penance by cursing another, rightly or wrongly, so forgiveness was the strength of ascetic Brahmanas.
shots.B14C092S36H03: Note 170: 'asat' is what does not exist, like a hare's horns; 'sadasat' is what exists and perishes; 'sadasat param' is the Unmanifest; all three come from Vasudeva.
shots.B14C092S36H04: Note 171: teachers in India taught without fee, and pupils gave a final Dakshina; Gautama is already satisfied with Utanka, so no gift is needed.
shots.B14C092S36H05: Note 172: the king's words are meant for his queen, who will understand: cursed by Vasishtha, he is a man-eater, and a gift of the ear-rings to a worthy Brahmana might bring merit to save him.
shots.B14C092S37H01: Note 173: another allusion to Vasishtha's curse; Madayanti is the king's only refuge, since her gift of the ear-rings to a worthy Brahmana may bring the merit he needs.
shots.B14C092S37H02: Note 174: a Brahmana is truthful, so Utanka will keep his word; acting falsely toward a friend is theft, which reminds the king not to harm him.
shots.B14C092S37H04: Note 176: 'chamu' here means a division, standing for an Akshauhini.
shots.B14C092S37H05: Note 177: 'Kavi' or 'Kavya' is another name for Sukra, the preceptor of the Daityas.
shots.B14C092S38H01: Note 178: 'Krishna' here means Vyasa, who was called the island-born Krishna.
shots.B14C092S38H02: Note 179: the constellation Dhruba means Rohini and the three Uttaras; Sunday is called the Dhruva-day.
shots.B14C092S38H03: Note 180: Agnivesya was another name for Dhaumya.
shots.B14C092S38H04: Note 181: the six roads run in two sets of three, north-south and east-west, dividing the camp into nine squares.
shots.B14C092S38H05: Note 182: a karaputa is a pair of wooden chests joined by chains or cords, carried by camels or bullocks.
shots.B14C092S39H01: Note 183: the first line of verse 17 is terse; literally, each vessel was joined to another, and each half of the load balanced on a scale.
shots.B14C092S39H03: Note 185: before a grave rite Hindus touch water to the lips, nostrils, ears and eyes, a rite called achamana.
shots.B14C092S39H04: Note 186: Vaisravana's abode is called Alaka; Vaisravana is Kubera, lord of treasure, friend of Mahadeva and chief of the Yakshas.
shots.B14C092S39H05: Note 187: the last line is slightly expanded in the translation.
shots.B14C092S40H01: Note 188: Yudhishthira is the eldest brother, so if he sacrifices his brothers are regarded as sacrificing with him.
shots.B14C092S40H02: Note 189: the sphya is a wooden sword used to slay the sacrificial animal, and the kurcha a handful of kusa grass; Vyasa directs that both be of pure gold.
shots.B14C092S40H03: Note 190: the Samsaptakas who fought Arjuna at Kurukshetra were Trigarta warriors led by Susarman, named for their oath to conquer or die.
shots.B14C092S40H04: Note 191: the translator reads 'Parthadupadravat' for 'Parthamupadravat', since the printed reading seems wrong.
shots.B14C092S40H05: Note 192: Bhagadatta was Indra's friend, and Indra was Arjuna's father.
shots.B14C092S41H01: Note 193: the allusion is to Mahadeva pursuing Sacrifice, who fled from him in the form of a deer.
shots.B14C092S41H02: Note 194: the Brahmanas were to receive Arjuna duly, and the treasure was offered as a mark of respect.
shots.B14C092S41H03: Note 195: Ulupi was one of Arjuna's wives, and so stepmother to Vabhruvahana.
shots.B14C092S41H04: Note 196: 'yahubharyyata', meaning polygamy in the first line, should be read as polyandry in the second, where the reference is to many husbands.
shots.B14C092S41H05: Note 197: to sit in Praya is to remain in one spot, abstaining from food and drink until one's life-breath leaves.
shots.B14C092S42H01: Note 198: grief does not kill; one dies only when one's hour comes, otherwise Ulupi's rival's affliction would have killed her.
shots.B14C092S42H02: Note 199: the name of the city was Suktimati.
shots.B14C092S42H03: Note 200: the etymology of Gudakesa as lord of sleep is fanciful.
shots.B14C092S42H04: Note 201: Sakuni was Duryodhana's maternal uncle, and so Arjuna's too, making Sakuni's son Arjuna's cousin.
shots.B14C092S42H05: Note 202: 'chara' does not always mean a spy; the ancient kings had spies and an intelligence service, whose successors were the harkaras of the Mughal period.
shots.B14C092S43H01: Note 203: hetuvadins are dialecticians who dispute the reasons for things.
shots.B14C092S43H02: Note 204: Krishna always called Draupadi his 'sakhi', or friend, showing a chivalry toward women at a time when they were held inferior.
shots.B14C092S43H03: Note 205: the Dakshina for the horse-sacrifice is fixed by rule, and Vyasa advises tripling it, which triples the sacrificer's merit.
shots.B14C092S43H04: Note 206: the Diksha is the initiation, in which mantras declare the intention to perform the sacrifice.
shots.B14C092S43H05: Note 207: the procedure follows the scriptures, and where they are silent it follows reasonable inference.
shots.B14C092S44H01: Note 208: Pravargya is a special preliminary rite; Abhishava is the pressing of Soma juice after it is consecrated with mantras.
shots.B14C092S44H02: Note 209: the woods are Vilwa (Aegle marmelos), Khadira (Acacia catechu), Saravarnin (Butea frondosa), Devadaru (Pinus deodara), and Sleshmataka, a small tree; some other tree may be meant here.
shots.B14C092S44H03: Note 210: the translator is unsure what the constructions were; they were probably figures drawn in gold-dust on the altar.
shots.B14C092S44H04: Note 211: each animal is matched to a particular deity.
shots.B14C092S44H05: Note 212: 'suvibhaktan' means properly grouped, so there was no dispute over precedence.
shots.B14C092S45H01: Note 213: Khandavaraga was made of long pepper, dried ginger, mung-bean juice and sugar, and is perhaps today's mungka laddu.
shots.B14C092S45H02: Note 214: the unccha vow means eating grains picked up after the harvest, as a pigeon does.
shots.B14C092S45H03: Note 215: the twelve-hour day is divided into eight divisions.
shots.B14C092S45H04: Note 216: a prastha is four kudavas, and a kudava is about twelve double handfuls.
shots.B14C092S45H05: Note 217: the verse is obscure; the translator reads it as the son urging his father to keep himself alive by taking his share, since the thought of an unfed guest would kill him.
shots.B14C092S46H01: Note 218: a daughter-in-law should be well treated for the good results every family seeks, so the father cannot deprive her of food.
shots.B14C092S46H02: Note 219: Diksha is the initiatory rite before a sacrifice or vow, lasting until the sacrifice or vow is complete.
shots.B14C092S46H03: Note 220: the Bombay text reads the first line differently, so that the sage creates the materials by thought alone.
shots.B14C092S46H04: Note 221: if penance yields great results, part of it is spent, and the Rishis did not want Agastya's penance used up on his sacrifice.
shots.B14C092S46H05: Note 222: the translator suspects the mongoose passage is an interpolation, perhaps invented so that Yudhishthira's great sacrifice would not be criticised, while noting that a small gift of barley under hardship is the nobler lesson.
shots.B14C092S47H03: Title block: attributed to Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa.
